Similarly, if we replace $\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ by $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{MU}}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ (and in particular $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ ), the analogue of the above composite admits a symmetric monoidal structure. In particular, if $M_{\bullet}$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -algebra in graded spectra (resp. graded $\mathrm{MU}$ - or $\mathbf{Z}$ -module spectra) which is concentrated in even weights, its “half-shear” $\widetilde{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}(M_{\bullet})$ admits an ${\mathbf{E}_{{\mathrm{min}(n,2)}}}$ -algebra structure in graded spectra (resp. ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -algebra structure in $\mathrm{MU}$ - or $\mathbf{Z}$ -module spectra).

Moreover, $\widetilde{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}:\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{F}_{2}}^{\mathrm{gr}}\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{F}_{2}}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ admits a symmetric monoidal structure. Indeed, there is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathbf{Z}^{\mathrm{ds}}\to\Pic(\mathbf{F}_{2})$ sending $1\mapsto\mathbf{F}_{2}[1]$ . There are many ways to see this; for instance, one can argue as in Lemma 2.1.3. Namely let $J_{\mathbf{R}}:\mathrm{BO}\times\mathbf{Z}^{\mathrm{ds}}\to\Pic(\mathrm{Sp})$ denote the real $J$ -homomorphism, so that $J_{\mathbf{R}}$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map, and $1\in\mathbf{Z}^{\mathrm{ds}}\mapsto S^{1}\in\Pic(\mathrm{Sp})$ . Since $\mathrm{MO}$ is the Thom spectrum of the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -composite $\mathrm{BO}\to\mathrm{BO}\times\mathbf{Z}^{\mathrm{ds}}\xrightarrow{{J_{\mathbf{R}}}}\Pic(\mathrm{Sp})$ , it can be understood as the initial ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $R$ equipped with a nullhomotopy of the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{BO}\xrightarrow{{J_{\mathbf{R}}}}\Pic(\mathrm{Sp})\to\Pic(R)$ . In particular, there is a commutative diagram of ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -maps:

$$ \textstyle{\mathrm{BO}\times\mathbf{Z}=\Omega^{\infty}\mathrm{ko}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{J_{\mathbf{R}}} \textstyle{\Pic(\mathrm{Sp})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\mathbf{Z}^{\mathrm{ds}}\simeq\Omega^{\infty}\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{ko}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\Pic(\mathrm{MO}).} $$

There is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -orientation $\mathrm{MO}\to\mathbf{F}_{2}$ , so we obtain an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathbf{Z}^{\mathrm{ds}}\to\Pic(\mathrm{MO})\to\Pic(\mathbf{F}_{2})$ sending $1\mapsto\mathbf{F}_{2}[1]$ , as desired.

The following observation will be useful below; in particular, the final sentence says that having polynomial homotopy generated by even-degree classes automatically forces “formality”, even as an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -algebra. For instance, for any compact torus $T$ , the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathbf{Z}$ -algebra $C^{\ast}(BT;\mathbf{Z})$ is “formal” as an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $\mathbf{Z}$ -algebra, i.e., $C^{\ast}(BT;\mathbf{Z})\simeq\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\pi_{\bullet}C^{\ast}(BT;\mathbf{Z})$ (More generally, the same is true of $C^{\ast}(BG;R)$ as long as $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BG;R)$ is a polynomial algebra on even classes.)

#### Lemma 2.1.10.

If $R$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathbf{F}_{2}$ -algebra, and $A$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebra such that $\pi_{\bullet}A$ is a finitely generated polynomial $R$ -algebra (whose generators need not live in even degrees), there is an equivalence $A\simeq{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}\pi_{\bullet}A$ of ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebras.

If $R$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring with even homotopy, and $A$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebra such that $\pi_{\bullet}A$ is a finitely generated polynomial $R$ -algebra generated by classes in even degrees, there is an equivalence $A\simeq{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}\pi_{\bullet}A$ of ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebras. If $A$ furthermore admits an ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ - $R$ -algebra structure, the equivalence $A\simeq{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}\pi_{\bullet}A$ can be upgraded to one of ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebras.

#### Proof.

Write $\pi_{\bullet}A\cong R[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n}]$ with $x_{j}$ in weight $2i_{j}$ . Observe that the shearing ${\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}R[x_{j}]$ is the free ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebra on a class in degree $2i_{j}$ . Similarly, if $R$ is an $\mathbf{F}_{2}$ -algebra and $y_{j}$ lives in weight $i_{j}$ , the shearing ${\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}R[y_{j}]$ is the free ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebra on a class in degree $i_{j}$ . This implies that there are ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebra maps ${\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}R[x_{j}]\to A$ for all $j$ such that $x_{j}$ is sent to the eponymous class on homotopy groups. Together, these define an ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebra map $\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n}{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}R[x_{j}]\to A^{\otimes n}\to A$ ; the first map is evidently one of ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebras, and the second map is one of ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebras since $A$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebra. By construction, this map induces an isomorphism on homotopy (and hence is an equivalence).

Now assume that $A$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ - $R$ -algebra such that $\pi_{\bullet}A$ is a finitely generated polynomial $R$ -algebra generated by classes in even degrees; we will first assume that $\pi_{\bullet}A\cong\pi_{\bullet}(R)[x_{2n}]$ with $x_{2n}$ in weight $2n$ . Let $R[x_{0,1}]=R[\mathbf{Z}_{\geq 0}]$ denote the flat graded polynomial $R$ -algebra on a class in weight $1$ and degree zero, so that $\widetilde{\mathrm{sh}}^{\circ n}(R)=R[x_{2n,1}]$ is a graded polynomial $R$ -algebra on a class in weight $1$ and degree $2n$ . By [DHL+, Corollary 3.12], $R[x_{2n,1}]$ admits the structure of a framed ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -algebra in $\mathrm{Mod}_{R}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ . Let $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])$ denote the underlying ungraded ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebra (in the body of this article, we will often simply omit “ $\mathrm{und}$ ”, but we keep it here for clarity), so that $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])$ is the free ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $R$ -algebra on a class in degree $2n$ . We will construct an equivalence $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])\xrightarrow{{\sim}}A$ of ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebras. For the case of multiple generators, note that if $\pi_{\bullet}(A)=\pi_{\bullet}(R)[x_{1},\cdots,x_{j}]$ , the above discussion produces an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebra map $\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n}{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}R[x_{j}]\to A^{\otimes n}\to A$ ; the first map is one of ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebras by assumption, and the second map is one of ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebras since $A$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ - $R$ -algebra. The map $\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n}{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}R[x_{j}]\to A$ is an isomorphism on homotopy, hence an equivalence, as desired.

Let us now return to the task of constructing an equivalence $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])\xrightarrow{{\sim}}A$ of ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebras. It suffices to show that $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])$ admits an even cell structure as an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $R$ -algebra (this does not require that $R$ have even homotopy!). Indeed, the class $x_{2n}\in\pi_{2n}(A)$ defines a map from the bottom ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -cell into $A$ ; all obstructions to extending this map along the higher ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -cells of $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])$ live in odd degrees, but the odd homotopy of $A$ vanishes, so such an extension $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])\to A$ exists. By construction, this map is an isomorphism on homotopy, and hence is an equivalence. To construct an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -cell structure for $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])$ , note that it in fact suffices to construct an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -cell structure for $R[x_{0,1}]$ in $\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}(\mathrm{Mod}_{R}^{\mathrm{gr}})$ : indeed, the desired ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -cell structure on $\mathrm{und}(R[x_{2n,1}])$ then follows from shearing and the fact that $\widetilde{\mathrm{sh}}$ is ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -monoidal by Construction 2.1.1. Since $R[x_{0,1}]$ is an augmented $R$ -algebra whose augmentation ideal is concentrated in positive weights, an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -cell structure for $R[x_{0,1}]$ is specified by a cell structure for the $2$ -fold bar construction $\Bar^{(2)}(R[x_{0,1}])$ . But this is a standard calculation: one finds that $\Bar^{(2)}(R[x_{0,1}])\simeq\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}R[2n](n)$ , at least as $R$ -modules. For a reference in slightly different language, see [Lur2, Proposition 3.4.5]. ∎

#### Remark 2.1.11.

In [DHL+, Remark 3.11], we show that $\widetilde{\mathrm{sh}}:\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{gr}}\to\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ cannot be made into an ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ -monoidal functor. This implies that in the setting of Lemma 2.1.10, even if $A$ admits an ${\mathbf{E}_{{4}}}$ - $R$ -algebra structure, the equivalence $A\simeq{\mathrm{sh}}^{1/2}\pi_{\bullet}A$ need not upgrade to an equivalence of ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ - $R$ -algebras. This is closely related to the subtlety of refining the derived geometric Satake equivalence (discussed in the present article as Theorem 3.2.7) into an ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ -monoidal equivalence.

#### Remark 2.1.12.

Being concerned with the relative Langlands program, it is important to understand whether Lemma 2.1.10 can be used to model maps between polynomial ring spectra, too. It is not too hard to show, for instance, that the map $C^{\ast}(BG;R)\to C^{\ast}(BH;R)$ induced by a homomorphism $H\to G$ can be modeled as the shearing of the induced map on cohomology when $R=\mathbf{Q}$ (both $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BG;R)$ and $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BH;R)$ are polynomial on even degree classes), and in the cases of $\mathrm{GL}_{n}\to\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}$ and $R=\mathbf{Z}$ , $\mathrm{SO}_{n}\to\mathrm{SO}_{n+1}$ when $R=\mathbf{F}_{2}$ or $R=\mathbf{Z}[1/2]$ , $\mathrm{O}_{n}\to\mathrm{GL}_{n}$ when $R=\mathbf{F}_{2}$ , etc.

However, there are examples where the map $C^{\ast}(BG;R)\to C^{\ast}(BH;R)$ cannot be modeled so naïvely; this should reflect subtle phenomena under Langlands duality at bad primes. For instance, consider the degree two map $\mathbf{G}_{m}\to\mathbf{G}_{m}^{(2)}$ with $R=\mathbf{F}_{2}$ . The homotopy fiber of the map $BS^{1}\to B(S^{1}/\mu_{2})$ is $B\mu_{2}\simeq\mathbf{R}P^{\infty}$ , and therefore

$$ C^{\ast}(BS^{1};\mathbf{F}_{2})\otimes_{C^{\ast}(B(S^{1}/\mu_{2});\mathbf{F}_{2})}\mathbf{F}_{2}\simeq C^{\ast}(\mathbf{R}P^{\infty};\mathbf{F}_{2}). $$

The induced map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(B(S^{1}/\mu_{2});\mathbf{F}_{2})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BS^{1};\mathbf{F}_{2})$ on cohomology rings is given by $\mathbf{F}_{2}[x]\to\mathbf{F}_{2}[y]$ , which necessarily sends $x$ to zero (indeed, the map on cohomology is the derivative of the map $\mathbf{G}_{m}\to\mathbf{G}_{m}^{(2)}$ at the identity, and the derivative of a square vanishes modulo $2$ ). This implies that there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BS^{1};\mathbf{F}_{2})\otimes_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(B(S^{1}/\mu_{2});\mathbf{F}_{2})}\mathbf{F}_{2}\cong\mathbf{F}_{2}[y,\sigma(x)]/(\sigma(x)^{2}). $$

The class $\sigma(x)$ lives in homological degree $-1$ . The Serre spectral sequence starts with the above tensor product and converges to the $\mathbf{F}_{2}$ -cohomology of $\mathbf{R}P^{\infty}$ ; this spectral sequence degenerates, but there is an interesting multiplicative extension $\sigma(x)^{2}=y$ on the $E_{\infty}$ -page (and this is proved using topological input invisible to the map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(B(S^{1}/\mu_{2});\mathbf{F}_{2})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BS^{1};\mathbf{F}_{2})$ ). One finds in conclusion that $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(B\mu_{2};\mathbf{F}_{2})\cong\mathbf{F}_{2}[\sigma(x)]$ , as expected.

### 2.2. Equivariant K-theory

Let $G$ be a compact Lie group. Atiyah and Segal constructed $G$ -equivariant K-theory using the theory of $G$ -equivariant vector bundles. We will review this theory here and describe the spectral algebro-geometric perspective on equivariant K-theory following [Lur1].

#### Definition 2.2.1.

A finite $G$ -space $X$ is a space with $G$ -action which is constructed from finitely many $G$ -cells of the form $G/H\times D^{n}$ , where $H\subseteq G$ is a closed subgroup. Let $\mathcal{S}(G)$ denote the $\infty$ -category of finite $G$ -spaces and $G$ -equivariant maps between them.

#### Definition 2.2.2.

Let $X$ be a finite $G$ -space. A $G$ -equivariant vector bundle on $X$ is a vector bundle $\mathcal{V}$ over $X$ equipped with a continuous $G$ -action, such that the map $\mathcal{V}\to X$ is $G$ -equivariant. Let $\mathrm{KU}_{G}^{0}(X)$ denote the Grothendieck group of the monoid of $G$ -equivariant vector bundles on $X$ .

Atiyah and Segal showed that the assignment $X\mapsto\mathrm{KU}_{G}^{0}(X)$ from the (opposite of the) homotopy category of finite $G$ -spaces to groups extends to a cohomology theory which is represented in the homotopy category of $G$ -spectra by a spectrum denoted by $\mathrm{KU}_{G}$ .

In order to see all the structure on equivariant K-theory, it will be convenient to phrase the construction in terms of the $\infty$ -category of orbispaces.

#### Definition 2.2.3.

Let $\mathchar 525$ denote the global orbit $\infty$ -category as defined in [GM, Definition 2.7]. Heuristically, this is the full subcategory of the $\infty$ -category of topological stacks spanned by objects of the form $\ast/G$ . An orbispace is a functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathrm{op}}\to{\mathcal{S}}$ . Let ${\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}$ denote the $\infty$ -category of orbispaces.

Let ${\mathcal{S}}_{G}$ denote the $\infty$ -category of $G$ -spaces, and let $\text{$\mathchar 525$}_{G}$ denote the full subcategory of ${\mathcal{S}}_{G}$ spanned by $G$ -spaces of the form $G/H$ with $H\subseteq G$ being a closed subgroup. By [GM, Proposition 2.16], there is a fully faithful functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}_{G}\to\text{$\mathchar 525$}_{/\ast/G}$ , whose essential image is spanned by those maps $\ast/H\to\ast/G$ which arise via an inclusion of subgroups $H\subseteq G$ .

#### Remark 2.2.4.

Note that $\mathcal{S}(G)$ is the full subcategory of ${\mathcal{S}}_{G}$ generated by $G$ -spaces of the form $G/H$ (for closed subgroups $H\subseteq G$ ) under finite colimits.

A more invariant construction of $\mathrm{KU}_{G}$ , along with its ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring structure, is as follows; see [GM, Section 4].

#### Construction 2.2.5.

Let $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L,st}})$ denote the functor sending $\ast/G\mapsto\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbf{C}}(G)$ . Taking connective additive K-theory, we obtain a functor $K:\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}$ . The functor $K$ is a module over the constant functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}$ sending $\ast/G\mapsto K(\mathrm{Vect}_{\mathbf{C}})\simeq\tau_{\geq 0}(\mathrm{KU})$ . Therefore, inverting the Bott class $\beta\in\pi_{2}\mathrm{KU}$ produces a functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{KU}}$ sending $\ast/G\mapsto\mathrm{KU}_{G}$ . Right Kan extending along the functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathrm{op}}\to{\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}^{\mathrm{op}}$ defines a lax symmetric monoidal functor ${\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{KU}}$ sending an orbispace $X/G\mapsto\mathrm{KU}_{G}(X)$ .

One important property of equivariant K-theory, which is also satisfied/posited to hold (depending on the construction) for equivariant analogues of other complex-oriented cohomology theories, is that it satisfies abelian descent. Let us review this, following [GM, Section 4].

#### Definition 2.2.6.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote a family of compact Lie groups (so that $\mathcal{A}$ is closed under isomorphisms, subgroups, and quotients). Define $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}$ to be the full subcategory of $\mathchar 525$ spanned by those $\ast/G$ with $G\in\mathcal{A}$ . For $\ast/G\in\text{$\mathchar 525$}$ , let $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}_{G}$ denote the full subcategory of $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}_{/\ast/G}$ spanned by those morphisms $\ast/H\to\ast/G$ which arise via an inclusion of subgroups $H\subseteq G$ . Note that by [GM, Proposition 2.16], one can identify $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}_{G}$ with the full subcategory of $\text{$\mathchar 525$}_{G}$ spanned by those $G/H$ with $H\in\mathcal{A}$ .

#### Theorem 2.2.7.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the family of abelian compact Lie groups. The functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{KU}}$ sending $\ast/G\mapsto\mathrm{KU}_{G}$ is right-Kan extended along the inclusion $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathrm{op}}$ .

#### Proof.

For each $\ast/G$ , one first notes that the inclusion $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}_{G}\to\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}_{/\ast/G}$ is final, so we need to show that the canonical map $\mathrm{KU}_{G}\to\lim_{\ast/H\in\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}_{G}}\mathrm{KU}_{H}$ is an equivalence. Let $E\mathcal{A}\simeq\colim_{G/H\in\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}_{G}}G/H$ , so that $E\mathcal{A}^{K}$ is empty if $K\not\in\mathcal{A}$ , and $E\mathcal{A}^{K}\simeq\ast$ if $K\in\mathcal{A}$ . In fact, this property characterizes $E\mathcal{A}$ up to weak equivalence. Then $\lim_{\ast/H\in\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}_{G}}\mathrm{KU}_{H}\simeq\mathrm{KU}_{G}(E\mathcal{A})$ , so we only need to show that the canonical map $\mathrm{KU}_{G}\to\mathrm{KU}_{G}(E\mathcal{A})$ is an equivalence. But this is [AHJM, Corollary 1.3]. ∎

#### Remark 2.2.8.

Instead of appealing to [AHJM, Corollary 1.3] in Theorem 2.2.7, one can argue explicitly as follows in the case when $G$ is connected with torsion-free $\pi_{1}(G)$ . Let $T$ be a maximal torus of $G$ , and let $G/T$ be the flag variety. If $H\subseteq G$ is a closed subgroup, $H$ is abelian if and only if some conjugate $gHg^{-1}$ is contained in $T$ , which in turn happens if and only if $(G/T)^{H}$ is nonempty. This implies that the $H$ -invariants of the geometric realization $|(G/T)^{\times\bullet+1}|$ is nonempty if and only if $H$ is abelian, in which case it is contractible. Therefore, by uniqueness of $E\mathcal{A}$ , there is a weak equivalence $E\mathcal{A}\simeq|(G/T)^{\times\bullet+1}|$ . This implies that

$$ \mathrm{KU}_{G}(E\mathcal{A})\simeq\Tot\mathrm{KU}_{G}((G/T)^{\times\bullet+1})\simeq\Tot\mathrm{KU}_{G}(G/T)^{\otimes_{\mathrm{KU}_{G}}\bullet+1}. $$

To conclude that this totalization is equivalent to $\mathrm{KU}_{G}$ by the unit map, it therefore suffices to show that the map $\mathrm{KU}_{G}\to\mathrm{KU}_{G}(G/T)$ induces a faithfully flat map on homotopy. But $\mathrm{KU}_{G}(G/T)=\mathrm{KU}_{T}$ , so by $2$ -periodicity, we only need to show that the map $R_{\mathbf{C}}(G)\to R_{\mathbf{C}}(T)$ on complex representation rings is faithfully flat. In fact, $R_{\mathbf{C}}(T)$ is a free $R_{\mathbf{C}}(G)$ -module by the main theorem of [Pit], thanks to our assumption that $G$ is connected with torsion-free $\pi_{1}$ .

#### Observation 2.2.9.

The ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{KU}$ -algebra $\mathrm{KU}_{T}$ is $2$ -periodic, with $\pi_{0}$ given by the complex representation ring $R_{\mathbf{C}}(T)$ . In particular, $\spec\pi_{0}\mathrm{KU}_{T}\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}[\mathbb{X}^{\ast}(T)]$ , where $\mathbb{X}^{\ast}(T)$ is the lattice of characters. This is precisely the algebraic group $\Hom(\mathbb{X}^{\ast}(T),\mathbf{G}_{m})$ .

#### Proposition 2.2.10.

Let $\mathbf{G}_{m,\mathrm{KU}}$ denote the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{KU}$ -scheme given by $\spec\mathrm{KU}[\mathbf{Z}]$ . Let $T$ be an abelian compact Lie group. Then there is an equivalence $\spec\mathrm{KU}_{T}\simeq\Hom(\mathbb{X}^{\ast}(T),\mathbf{G}_{m,\mathrm{KU}})$ .

#### Variant 2.2.11.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the family of abelian compact Lie groups. Let $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}\to\mathrm{Sch}_{/\mathrm{KU}}$ denote the functor to spectral schemes over $\mathrm{KU}$ sending $\ast/T\mapsto\spec\mathrm{KU}_{T}$ . That this is well-defined is essentially [GM, Proposition 4.4]. The left Kan extension of this functor along the inclusion $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}\hookrightarrow\text{$\mathchar 525$}$ defines a functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}\to\mathrm{Sch}_{/\mathrm{KU}}$ , which, by Theorem 2.2.7, sends $\ast/G\mapsto\spec\mathrm{KU}_{G}$ . Further left Kan extending along the inclusion $\text{$\mathchar 525$}\to{\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}$ defines a functor ${\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}\to\mathrm{Sch}_{/\mathrm{KU}}$ sending $X/G\mapsto\spec\mathrm{KU}_{G}(X)$ .

#### Remark 2.2.12.

This construction can be extended further. Namely, consider the composite $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sch}_{/\mathrm{KU}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{LinCat}_{\mathrm{KU}})$ , where the functor $\mathrm{Sch}_{/\mathrm{KU}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{LinCat}_{\mathrm{KU}})$ is given by taking quasicoherent sheaves. Right Kan extending this functor along the inclusion $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{op}}\to{\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}^{\mathrm{op}}$ defines a functor ${\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{LinCat}_{\mathrm{KU}})$ , which we will denote by $X/G\mapsto\mathrm{Loc}_{G}(X;\mathrm{KU})$ . The $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{G}(X;\mathrm{KU})$ could (somewhat abusively) be called the $\infty$ -category of $G$ -equivariant local systems of $\mathrm{KU}$ -modules on $X$ . We will not use this notion below.

#### Remark 2.2.13.

The functor ${\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}\to\mathrm{Sch}_{/\mathrm{KU}}$ refines to a functor $({\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}})_{/\ast/G}\to\mathrm{Sch}_{/\mathrm{KU}_{G}}$ . In particular, if $X$ is a space with $G$ -action, and $X/G$ denotes the associated orbispace (so that $X/G\in({\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}})_{/\ast/G}$ ), there is a canonical map $\spec\mathrm{KU}_{G}(X)\to\spec\mathrm{KU}_{G}$ . We will often write $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)$ to denote the associated ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{KU}_{G}$ -algebra.

### 2.3. Equivariant connective K-theory

We will need a good theory of equivariant connective K-theory. (This is not the functor $K$ of Construction 2.2.5.) It will be most convenient to adopt the spectral algebro-geometric perspective of Variant 2.2.11. To motivate the construction, let us briefly recall the definition of nonequivariant connective K-theory.

#### Definition 2.3.1.

Let $\mathrm{ku}$ denote the connective cover of complex K-theory $\mathrm{KU}$ . Then $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}\cong\mathbf{Z}[\beta]$ with $|\beta|=2$ , so that $\mathrm{ku}[\beta^{-1}]=\mathrm{KU}$ , and $\mathrm{ku}/\beta\simeq\mathbf{Z}$ .

Let us suggest some desiderata in the simple case of $S^{1}$ -equivariance.

#### Expectation 2.3.2.

By construction, there is an isomorphism $\spec\mathrm{KU}_{S^{1}}\simeq\mathbf{G}_{m,\mathrm{KU}}$ of spectral schemes over $\mathrm{KU}$ . Recall that $\spec\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BS^{1};\mathbf{Z})\cong\hat{\mathbf{G}}_{a}(2)$ as graded $\mathbf{Z}$ -schemes, where the coordinate of $\hat{\mathbf{G}}_{a}$ lives in weight $-2$ . This can also be identified with the graded $\mathbf{Z}$ -scheme $\spec\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})=\mathbf{G}_{a}(2)$ , since equipping the coordinate on $\mathbf{G}_{a}$ with the nonzero weight $-2$ allows us to identify $\hat{\mathbf{G}}_{a}(2)\cong\mathbf{G}_{a}(2)$ . Therefore, if $\mathbf{Z}_{S^{1}}$ denotes the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathbf{Z}$ -algebra representing $S^{1}$ -equivariant $\mathbf{Z}$ -cohomology, one expects the appropriate notion of $S^{1}$ -equivariant connective K-theory $\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}$ to be a sufficiently structured $\mathrm{ku}$ -algebra such that there is a diagram where each square is Cartesian:

$$ \textstyle{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\mathbf{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{(\mathbf{G}_{m})_{\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\pm 1}]}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Z}_{S^{1}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{KU}_{S^{1}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\spec\mathbf{Z}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\spec\mathbf{Z}[\beta]} \textstyle{\spec\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\pm 1}]\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} $$

In particular, one expects that there is an isomorphism of graded $\mathbf{Z}[\beta]$ -group schemes

$$ \spec\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}[\beta][x,\tfrac{1}{1+\beta x}], $$

where $x$ lives in weight $-2$ and the group structure is given by $x\mapsto x\otimes 1+1\otimes x+\beta x\otimes x$ .

Let us recall a construction of the group scheme $\spec\mathbf{Z}[\beta][x,\tfrac{1}{1+\beta x}]$ .

#### Recollection 2.3.3.

Let $\mathbf{Z}[y]$ denote the graded $\mathbf{Z}$ -algebra where $y$ has weight $1$ . The $(t-1)$ -adically filtered ring $\mathbf{Z}[t^{\pm 1}]$ defines a commutative algebra object $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mathrm{fil}}$ , which, by the Rees construction $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}[y]}^{\mathrm{gr}}\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mathrm{fil}}$ , defines a commutative algebra object of $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}[y]}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ . This algebra is simply $\mathbf{Z}[y][t^{\pm 1},\tfrac{t-1}{y}]$ . The shearing autoequivalence of $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ sending $M_{\bullet}\mapsto M_{\bullet}[2\bullet]$ sends $\mathbf{Z}[y]$ to a graded ring $\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\prime}]$ with $\beta^{\prime}$ in weight $1$ and degree $2$ , so that shearing defines an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mathrm{fil}}\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}[y]}^{\mathrm{gr}}\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\prime}]}^{\mathrm{gr}}. $$

Under this equivalence, the $(t-1)$ -adically filtered ring $\mathbf{Z}[t^{\pm 1}]$ is sent to the graded $\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\prime}]$ -algebra $\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\prime},t^{\pm 1},\tfrac{t-1}{\beta^{\prime}}]$ .

We will adapt essentially the same argument to the spectral setting, with some minor homotopical issues complicating the story.

#### Proposition 2.3.4 ([Mou1]).

The ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{MU}$ -algebra $\mathrm{MU}[y]$ (with $y$ in degree zero) admits a grading where $y$ is in weight $1$ . There is a symmetric monoidal equivalence $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{MU}[y]}^{\mathrm{gr}}\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{MU}}^{\mathrm{fil}}$ . In particular, if $\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}]$ denotes the graded ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{MU}$ -algebra given by the shearing of $\mathrm{MU}[y]$ (so that $\beta^{\prime}$ lives in degree $2$ and weight $1$ ), Lemma 2.1.3 defines a symmetric monoidal equivalence $\mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}:\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{MU}}^{\mathrm{fil}}\xrightarrow{{\sim}}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}]}^{\mathrm{gr}}$ .

#### Lemma 2.3.5.

Let $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])$ denote the ungraded ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{MU}$ -algebra which underlies $\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}]$ . There is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{MU}$ -algebra map $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])\to\mathrm{ku}$ sending $\beta^{\prime}\mapsto\beta$ .

#### Proof.

Note that by construction, $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])$ can be identified with the Thom spectrum of the composite

$$ \mathrm{BU}\times\mathbf{Z}_{\geq 0}\to\mathrm{BU}\times\mathbf{Z}\xrightarrow{{J}}\Pic(\mathrm{Sp}). $$

Let $\mathrm{MU}_{\mathrm{per}}$ denote the Thom spectrum of the map $J:\mathrm{BU}\times\mathbf{Z}\to\Pic(\mathrm{Sp})$ . Then there is a canonical map $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])\to\mathrm{MU}_{\mathrm{per}}$ . There is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{MU}_{\mathrm{per}}\to\mathrm{KU}$ which sends $\mathrm{oblv}(\beta^{\prime})\in\pi_{2}\mathrm{MU}_{\mathrm{per}}$ to the Bott class (see, e.g., [HJN+, Remark 6.3]), and hence an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])\to\mathrm{KU}$ . which does the same. But $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])$ is connective, so this map factors through an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])\to\mathrm{ku}$ , as desired. ∎

#### Construction 2.3.6.

Let $I$ denote the fiber of the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{MU}[t^{\pm 1}]\to\mathrm{MU}$ given by $\mathrm{MU}$ -chains of the map $\mathbf{Z}\to\ast$ . Then the functor $\mathbf{Z}_{\geq 0}\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{MU}}$ sending $n\mapsto I^{\otimes_{\mathrm{MU}[t^{\pm 1}]}n}$ defines an object $\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{(t-1)}\mathrm{MU}[t^{\pm 1}]\in\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{MU}}^{\mathrm{fil}})$ . Applying the symmetric monoidal equivalence of Proposition 2.3.4, we obtain a graded ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}]$ -algebra $\mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}(\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{(t-1)}\mathrm{MU}[t^{\pm 1}])$ . Note that this graded ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}]$ -algebra admits a strictly cocommutative ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{MU}$ -coalgebra structure by the map $t\mapsto t\otimes t$ .

Let $\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}$ denote the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}$ -bialgebra given by

$$ \mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}:=\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}(\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{(t-1)}\mathrm{MU}[t^{\pm 1}]))\otimes_{\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])}\mathrm{ku}, $$

where the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime}])\to\mathrm{ku}$ is given by Lemma 2.3.5. We will write $\spec\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}$ , or sometimes $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{ku},\beta}$ , to denote the functor $\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}}\to{\mathcal{S}}$ which is corepresented by $\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}$ . Since $\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}$ is a strictly cocommutative ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}$ -coalgebra, this functor in fact lands in the $\infty$ -category $s\mathrm{Ab}$ of simplicial abelian groups. We will write $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ to denote the underlying graded $\pi_{\ast}(\mathrm{ku})=\mathbf{Z}[\beta]$ -scheme.

#### Remark 2.3.7.

By comparison to Recollection 2.3.3, it is not difficult to see that

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}(\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{(t-1)}\mathrm{MU}[t^{\pm 1}])\cong\pi_{\ast}(\mathrm{MU})[\beta^{\prime},t^{\pm 1},\tfrac{t-1}{\beta^{\prime}}], $$

where $\beta^{\prime}$ is in weight $1$ and degree $2$ , and $\tfrac{t-1}{\beta^{\prime}}$ is in weight $-1$ and degree $-2$ . Therefore,

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}\cong\mathbf{Z}[\beta][t^{\pm 1},\tfrac{t-1}{\beta}], $$

as expressed in Expectation 2.3.2.

#### Remark 2.3.8.

Note that if we invert the Bott class in $\pi_{2}\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}$ , we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}[\beta^{-1}] \displaystyle=\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}(\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{(t-1)}\mathrm{MU}[t^{\pm 1}])[\beta^{\prime-1}])\otimes_{\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime\pm 1}])}\mathrm{KU} \displaystyle\simeq\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime\pm 1}][t^{\pm 1}]\otimes_{\mathrm{MU}[\beta^{\prime\pm 1}]}\mathrm{KU}\simeq\mathrm{KU}[t^{\pm 1}]=\mathrm{KU}_{S^{1}}, $$

as expressed in Expectation 2.3.2.

#### Observation 2.3.9.

It is not difficult to extend the above construction to arbitary abelian compact Lie groups $T$ . Namely, given a functor $F:\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}}\to s\mathrm{Ab}$ and an abelian compact Lie group $T$ , one obtains a new functor $F_{T}:\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}}\to s\mathrm{Ab}$ given by $\Hom(\mathbb{X}^{\ast}(T),F)$ . If $F$ is corepresentable, the same is true of $F_{T}$ . Applied to the functor $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{ku},\beta}:\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}}\to s\mathrm{Ab}$ , we obtain an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}$ -algebra $\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ . This assignment evidently defines a functor from the $\infty$ -category of abelian compact Lie groups to ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}$ -algebras. We will write the underlying graded group $\mathbf{Z}[\beta]$ -scheme of $\spec\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ as $T_{\beta}$ .

In order to extend the functoriality of the assignment $T\mapsto\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ , we need the following.

#### Lemma 2.3.10.

There is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}$ -algebra map $\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}\to\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}$ which is given on homotopy by the map

$$ \mathbf{Z}[\beta][t^{\pm 1},\tfrac{t-1}{\beta}]\to\mathbf{Z}[\beta][\![\hbar]\!]\cong\mathbf{Z}[\![t-1]\!][\beta][\![\hbar]\!]/(\beta\hbar=t-1) $$

sending $\tfrac{t-1}{\beta}\mapsto\hbar$ .

#### Proof.

The orientation of the spectral formal multiplicative group $\hat{\mathbf{G}}_{m}$ over $\mathrm{KU}$ defines an equivalence of ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -rings $\mathrm{KU}^{hS^{1}}\xrightarrow{{\sim}}\mathrm{KU}[\![t-1]\!]$ (see [Lur4, Sections 4.4 and 6.5]), where the map sends $\beta\hbar\mapsto t-1$ on $\pi_{0}$ . This defines a canonical ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $S[\![t-1]\!]\to\mathrm{KU}^{hS^{1}}$ , which can be interpreted as a $BS^{1}$ -family of ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $S[\![t-1]\!]\to\mathrm{KU}$ . Since $S[\![t-1]\!]$ is connective, this is the same as a $BS^{1}$ -family of ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -maps $S[\![t-1]\!]\to\mathrm{ku}$ , i.e., an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $S[\![t-1]\!]\to\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}$ .

This defines an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{ku}[t^{\pm 1}]\to\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}$ via the $\mathrm{ku}$ -linearization of the composite

$$ S[t^{\pm 1}]\to S[\![t-1]\!]\to\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}. $$

Note that the pushout $\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}\otimes_{S[t^{\pm 1}]}S$ equips $\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}/\beta\hbar$ with the structure of an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}$ -algebra. Let $J$ denote the fiber of the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}\to\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}/\beta\hbar$ , so that $\pi_{\ast}J$ is the ideal of $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}=\mathbf{Z}[\beta][\![\hbar]\!]$ generated by $\beta\hbar$ . Let $\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{\beta\hbar}\mathrm{ku}$ denote the filtered ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $J^{\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}}\ast}$ . The above discussion produces a map $\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{(t-1)}\mathrm{ku}[t^{\pm 1}]\to\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{\beta\hbar}\mathrm{ku}$ of filtered ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}$ -algebras, and hence a map

$$ \mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}(\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{(t-1)}\mathrm{ku}[t^{\pm 1}])\to\mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}(\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{\beta\hbar}\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}) $$

of graded ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}[\beta^{\prime}]$ -algebras. In particular, applying $\mathrm{oblv}$ and base-changing along the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}$ -algebra map $\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{ku}[\beta^{\prime}])\to\mathrm{ku}$ from Lemma 2.3.5 defines a map of ungraded ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}(\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{(t-1)}\mathrm{ku}[t^{\pm 1}]))\otimes_{\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{ku}[\beta^{\prime}])}\mathrm{ku}\to\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{Rees}_{\beta^{\prime}}(\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{\beta\hbar}\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}))\otimes_{\mathrm{oblv}(\mathrm{ku}[\beta^{\prime}])}\mathrm{ku}. $$

But it is not difficult to see that the target is precisely $\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}}$ . ∎

#### Proposition 2.3.11.

The group scheme $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{ku},\beta}$ is preoriented (compatibly with the orientation on $\mathbf{G}_{m,\mathrm{KU}}$ ), and the construction from Observation 2.3.9 extends to a functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}\to\Fun(\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}},{\mathcal{S}})$ sending $T\mapsto\spec\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ .

#### Proof.

Following [GM, Construction 3.13 and Proposition 4.4], the desired functor can be defined as follows. First, note that the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map of Lemma 2.3.10 defines a map

$$ \mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}}}(\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}},\mathrm{ku})\to\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}}}(\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}},\mathrm{ku})=\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{ku},\beta}(\mathrm{ku}). $$

There is an obvious map

$$ {\mathbf{C}P}^{\infty}\to\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}}}(\mathrm{ku}^{hS^{1}},\mathrm{ku}) $$

of simplicial abelian groups. The resulting map ${\mathbf{C}P}^{\infty}\to\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{ku},\beta}(\mathrm{ku})$ defines a preorientation $\ast/S^{1}\to\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{ku},\beta}$ , and hence a functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}\times\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}}\to{\mathcal{S}}$ sending

$$ (X,R)\mapsto\mathrm{Map}_{s\mathrm{Ab}_{\ast/S^{1}/}}(\mathrm{Map}(X,\ast/S^{1}),\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{ku},\beta}(R)). $$

This is adjoint to the desired functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}\to\Fun(\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}},{\mathcal{S}})$ . It is not difficult to see that this functor sends $T\mapsto\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ . ∎

Motivated by Variant 2.2.11, we are led to:

#### Definition 2.3.12.

Let ${\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}\to\Fun(\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}},{\mathcal{S}})$ denote the functor given by left Kan extending the functor $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}\to\Fun(\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}},{\mathcal{S}})$ along the inclusion $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A}}\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}$ . It is not hard to see that this functor in fact lands in the full subcategory spanned by the representable functors, so we will denote this functor by $X/G\mapsto\spec\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)$ . The functor ${\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}\to\Fun(\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}},{\mathcal{S}})$ refines to a functor $({\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}})_{/\ast/G}\to\Fun(\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}},{\mathcal{S}})$ . In particular, if $X$ is a space with $G$ -action, and $X/G$ denotes the associated orbispace (so that $X/G\in({\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}})_{/\ast/G}$ ), there is a canonical map $\spec\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)\to\spec\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ . We will write $\mathrm{ku}^{\ast}_{G}(X)$ to denote $\pi_{-\ast}\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)$ .

#### Remark 2.3.13.

This construction can be extended further. Namely, consider the composite $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{op}}\to\Fun(\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}},{\mathcal{S}})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{LinCat}_{\mathrm{ku}})$ , where the functor $\Fun(\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}},{\mathcal{S}})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{LinCat}_{\mathrm{ku}})$ is given by taking quasicoherent sheaves. Right Kan extending this functor along the inclusion $\text{$\mathchar 525$}^{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{op}}\to{\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}^{\mathrm{op}}$ defines a functor ${\mathcal{S}}_{\text{$\mathchar 525$}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{LinCat}_{\mathrm{ku}})$ , which we will denote by $X/G\mapsto\mathrm{Loc}_{G}(X;\mathrm{ku})$ . The $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{G}(X;\mathrm{ku})$ could (somewhat abusively) be called the $\infty$ -category of $G$ -equivariant local systems of $\mathrm{ku}$ -modules on $X$ . We will not use this notion below.

#### Notation 2.3.14.

Let $\mathcal{M}_{G}$ denote the underlying graded $\mathbf{Z}[\beta]$ -scheme of $\spec\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ , i.e., $\mathcal{M}_{G}=\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ .

#### Proposition 2.3.15.

Let $G$ be a connected compact Lie group such that $\pi_{1}(G)$ is torsion-free, and let $T\subseteq G$ be a maximal torus with associated Weyl group $W$ . Let $X/G$ be an orbispace over $\ast/G$ , and let $X/T$ denote the associated orbispace of $\ast/T$ . Upon inverting $|W|$ , the natural map $\spec\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\spec\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)$ exhibits the graded scheme $\spec\mathrm{ku}^{\ast}_{G}(X)$ as the GIT quotient $\spec\mathrm{ku}^{\ast}_{T}(X)/\!\!/W$ . In particular, $\mathcal{M}_{G}\cong T_{\beta}/\!\!/W$ .

#### Proof.

Following Remark 2.2.8, we can identify $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)$ with the totalization of the diagram

$$ \mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\rightrightarrows\mathcal{F}_{T}(X\times G/T){\begin{subarray}{c}\rightarrow\\[-10.00002pt]
\rightarrow\\[-10.00002pt]
\rightarrow\end{subarray}}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X\times G/T\times G/T)\cdots $$

There is an isomorphism $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X\times G/T)\simeq\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}_{T}}\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T)$ . We will argue the case $X=\ast$ below; the general case is no more difficult.

To understand $\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T)$ , we will use Proposition 2.4.10. This is classical: $(G/T)^{T}=W$ , so the set $V$ of vertices of the GKM diagram is given by $V=W$ . The edges in the GKM diagram are indexed by positive roots $\alpha\in\Phi^{+}$ : the edge labelled by $\alpha$ connects the vertices $w\mapsto s_{\alpha}w$ . It follows that there is an equalizer diagram

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Map}(W,\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T})\rightrightarrows\prod_{(w,\alpha)}\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T_{\alpha}}, $$

where $T_{\alpha}$ is the kernel of the map $\alpha:T\to S^{1}$ . Said differently, the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}}\mathcal{F}_{T}\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T)$ defines a closed immersion $\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T)\hookrightarrow T_{\beta}\times_{\spec\mathbf{Z}[\beta]}T_{\beta}$ which exhibits $\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T)$ as the union of graphs of $W$ acting on $T_{\beta}$ . Let us denote this union of graphs by $\mathcal{U}_{W}$ .

Now, if $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T)$ is flat over $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ , there is an isomorphism $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}((G/T)^{\times k+1})\cong(\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T))^{\otimes_{\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}}k}$ . The assumption that $\pi_{1}(G)$ is torsion-free implies (by [Pit]) that $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}^{(G/T)_{+}}$ is flat (in fact free) over $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}$ , from which the desired flatness of $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T)$ over $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ follows. We find that $\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ can be expressed as the geometric realization of the simplicial diagram

$$ \spec\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}((G/T)^{\times\bullet+1})\cong\spec(\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(G/T))^{\times_{\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}}\bullet}\cong\mathcal{U}_{W}^{\times_{T_{\beta}}\bullet}. $$

Let us now invert $|W|$ . The map $T_{\beta}\to T_{\beta}/\!\!/W$ is faithfully flat (by [Pit]). The argument of [Gan, Proposition A.2] shows that $T_{\beta}\times_{T_{\beta}/\!\!/W}T_{\beta}\cong\mathcal{U}_{W}$ : it is true after inverting $\beta$ (even if $|W|$ is not inverted) by [Gan, Remark A.3], and when $\beta=0$ , it follows from [Gan, Proposition A.2]. (This result applies in the present situation because $|W|$ is inverted, and so the Chevalley-Shephard-Todd theorem continues to hold for the map $\mathfrak{t}\to\mathfrak{t}/\!\!/W$ .) The geometric realization of the above simplicial diagram can therefore be identified with $T_{\beta}/\!\!/W$ , as desired. ∎

### 2.4. Equivariant $\mathrm{ku}$ -homology

The goal of this section is to set up the theory of equivariant $\mathrm{ku}$ -homology. Fix a compact Lie group $G$ throughout.

#### Definition 2.4.1.

Let $\mathcal{F}_{G}(-)^{\vee}:{\mathcal{S}}(G)\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ denote the functor given by sending $X/G\mapsto\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)^{\vee}$ , where $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)^{\vee}$ denotes the $\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)$ . We will refer to $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)^{\vee}$ as the $G$ -equivariant $\mathrm{ku}$ -homology of $X$ , and often write the homotopy groups of this spectrum as $\mathrm{ku}^{G}_{\ast}(X)$ .

#### Remark 2.4.2.

Note that the functor $\mathcal{F}_{G}(-)^{\vee}:{\mathcal{S}}(G)\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ is in fact symmetric monoidal. Since every $G$ -space is naturally equipped with a diagonal map, this refines $\mathcal{F}_{G}(-)^{\vee}$ to a functor ${\mathcal{S}}(G)\to\mathrm{coCAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ .

The above definition is badly behaved if $X$ is not a finite $G$ -space. This is not special to the equivariant setting, as the following example shows.

#### Example 2.4.3.

The integral cohomology of the discrete space $\mathbf{Z}$ is given by the ring $\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{Z},\mathbf{Z})$ of all functions $\mathbf{Z}\to\mathbf{Z}$ . Given such a function $f$ , one can define a new function $\Delta f:\mathbf{Z}\to\mathbf{Z}$ via $f(x+1)-f(x)$ . Then, we formally have $f(x)=\sum_{k\geq 0}(\Delta^{k}f)(0)\binom{x}{k}$ . This series converges in the completion of the ring $\mathbf{Z}[\binom{x}{k}]_{k\geq 0}$ of numerical polynomials. However, the $\mathbf{Z}$ -linear dual of $\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{Z},\mathbf{Z})$ is not isomorphic to the group algebra $\mathbf{Z}[t^{\pm 1}]=\mathbf{Z}[\mathbf{Z}]=\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\mathbf{Z};\mathbf{Z})$ .

The basic issue is the infinitude of $\mathbf{Z}$ , which leads to a difference between $\mathbf{Z}^{\mathbf{Z}}$ and $\mathbf{Z}^{\oplus\mathbf{Z}}$ . The simplest fix is to observe that $\mathbf{Z}$ admits a filtration by finite subsets $I_{n}=\{-n,\cdots,n\}$ , and that $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(I_{n};\mathbf{Z})=\mathbf{Z}\{t^{-n},\cdots,t^{n}\}$ is indeed the $\mathbf{Z}$ -linear dual of $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(I_{n};\mathbf{Z})=\mathrm{Map}(I_{n},\mathbf{Z})$ . Note that this filtration of $\mathbf{Z}$ equips it with the structure of a filtered group: namely, the addition on $\mathbf{Z}$ gives maps $I_{n}\times I_{m}\to I_{n+m}$ for each $n,m\in\mathbf{Z}$ .

We will therefore rely on the following construction.

#### Construction 2.4.4.

Let $\mathcal{F}_{G}(-)^{\vee}:{\mathcal{S}}_{G}\to\mathrm{coCAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ denote the left Kan extension of the functor ${\mathcal{S}}(G)\to\mathrm{coCAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ along the inclusion ${\mathcal{S}}(G)\to{\mathcal{S}}_{G}$ . Explicitly, if $X\in{\mathcal{S}}_{G}$ is a $G$ -space equipped with a presentation $X=\colim_{j\in\mathcal{J}}X_{j}$ as the filtered colimit of a filtered diagram $\mathcal{J}\to{\mathcal{S}}(G)$ of finite $G$ -spaces, then $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)^{\vee}$ is the filtered colimit $\colim_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mathcal{F}_{G}(X_{j})^{\vee}$ ; we will refer to it as the $G$ -equivariant $\mathrm{ku}$ -homology of $X$ . Note that the forgetful functor $\mathrm{coCAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ preserves colimits, so this filtered colimit can be computed in $\mathrm{coCAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ or $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ .

In most examples of interest, there will be a geometrically defined presentation of $X$ .

#### Remark 2.4.5.

Let $X$ be a finite $G$ -space equipped with an ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -algebra structure in $G$ -spaces. Then $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)^{\vee}$ admits an ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -algebra structure in $\mathrm{coCAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ . If $X$ is not a finite $G$ -space, but is equipped with an ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -algebra structure in ${\mathcal{S}}_{G}$ , the definition of $G$ -equivariant $\mathrm{ku}$ -homology via Construction 2.4.4 does not guarantee the existence of an ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -algebra structure on $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)^{\vee}\in\mathrm{coCAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ . Rather, if $\mathcal{J}$ is a filtered index category equipped with an ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -monoidal structure and $\mathcal{J}\to{\mathcal{S}}_{G}$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -algebra object in the $\infty$ -category $\Fun(\mathcal{J},{\mathcal{S}}_{G})$ equipped with the Day convolution monoidal structure, Construction 2.4.4 will define an ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -algebra structure on $\mathcal{F}_{G}(X)^{\vee}\in\mathrm{coCAlg}_{\mathrm{ku}_{G}}$ . We will refer to such a presentation of $X$ as a multiplicative presentation.

A basic fact about equivariant connective K-theory is the localization theorem. Although one can make statements about $\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ for arbitrary compact Lie groups $G$ , we will restrict attention only to the case when $G=T$ is an abelian compact Lie group. In this case, we have the following simple observation.

#### Lemma 2.4.6.

Let $T$ be an abelian compact Lie group, and let $X$ be a finite $T$ -space. Let $T_{0}\subseteq T$ be a closed subgroup, and let $\mathcal{U}_{T_{0}}\subseteq T_{\beta}$ denote the complement of the union of the closed subschemes $T^{\prime}_{\beta}$ ranging over all closed subgroups $T^{\prime}\subseteq T$ which do not contain $T_{0}$ . Then the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T_{0}})$ , and hence the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T_{0}})^{\vee}\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)^{\vee}$ , is an equivalence upon restriction to $\mathcal{U}_{T_{0}}$ .

#### Proof.

By induction on the orbit stratification on $X$ , we are reduced to the case when $X=T/T_{1}$ for some closed subgroup $T_{1}\subseteq T$ . In this case, the fixed points $X^{T_{0}}$ is empty if $T_{0}\not\subseteq T_{1}$ , and $X^{T_{0}}=X$ if $T_{0}\subseteq T_{1}$ . It therefore suffices to show that $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)|_{T_{\beta}-T_{1,\beta}}=0$ if $T_{0}\not\subseteq T_{1}$ ; but this is clear, because $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\cong\mathcal{O}_{T_{1,\beta}}$ . ∎

#### Remark 2.4.7.

One special case of Lemma 2.4.6 which is worth restating (coresponding to $T_{0}=T$ ) is the following. Let ${T}^{\circ}_{\beta}$ denote the complement of the union of the closed subscheme $T^{\prime}_{\beta}$ ranging over all closed proper subgroups $T^{\prime}\subsetneq T$ . Then the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})$ , and hence the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})^{\vee}\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)^{\vee}$ , is an equivalence upon restriction to ${T}^{\circ}_{\beta}$ .

#### Lemma 2.4.8.

Let $T$ be a torus, and let $X$ be a finite $T$ -space. If $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)$ is a projective $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ -module, the map $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})$ is an injection.

#### Proof.

Since the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})_{{T}^{\circ}_{\beta}}$ factors as $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)|_{{T}^{\circ}_{\beta}}\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})|_{{T}^{\circ}_{\beta}}$ , and the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)|_{{T}^{\circ}_{\beta}}\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})|_{{T}^{\circ}_{\beta}}$ is an equivalence by Lemma 2.4.6, it suffices to show that the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)|_{{T}^{\circ}_{\beta}}$ induces an injection on homotopy groups. But $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)$ was assumed to be a projective $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ -module, so one is reduced to the case $X=\ast$ , i.e., to showing that the map $\mathrm{ku}_{T}\to\mathrm{ku}_{T}|_{{T}^{\circ}_{\beta}}$ induces an injection on homotopy groups. This, however, is clear, since the closed subscheme $T^{\prime}_{\beta}\hookrightarrow T_{\beta}$ defined by each closed subgroup $T^{\prime}\subseteq T$ is cut out by a regular sequence. ∎

#### Definition 2.4.9.

Let $X$ be a finite $T$ -space equipped with a chosen presentation in terms of $T$ -cells. Say that $X$ is a GKM space if the following conditions are satisfied:

- • $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)$ is a projective $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ -module;

- • if $X^{(1)}$ denotes the equivariant $1$ -skeleton of $X$ , then $X^{(1)}$ consists of a finite number of spheres $S^{\lambda}$ meeting only at the fixed points, where $\lambda$ ranges over characters of $T$ .

Let $V$ denote the set $X^{T}$ of fixed points, and let $E$ denote the set of characters $\lambda$ such that $S^{\lambda}\subseteq X^{(1)}$ . There are two maps $E\rightrightarrows V$ sending $\lambda$ to the points $0,\infty\in S^{\lambda}\subseteq X^{(1)}$ .

#### Proposition 2.4.10 (Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson).

Let $X$ be a finite GKM $T$ -space equipped with a chosen presentation in terms of $T$ -cells. For each character $\lambda:T\to S^{1}$ , let $T_{\lambda}$ denote the kernel of $T$ , and let $S(\lambda)$ denote the unit representation sphere, so that $\mathrm{ku}_{T_{\lambda}}\cong\mathcal{F}_{T}(S(\lambda))$ . Then there is an equalizer diagram

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\hookrightarrow\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})\cong\mathrm{Map}(V,\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T})\rightrightarrows\prod_{\lambda\in E}\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T_{\lambda}}, $$

where the two maps in the equalizer are defined in the evident manner.

A general version of the Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson theorem is proved in [HHH].

#### Proof.

Let us first show that the maps $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})$ and $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{(1)})\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})$ have the same images on homotopy. There is an evident map from the image of $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})$ on homotopy to the image of $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{(1)})\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})$ on homotopy, which we will denote by $f$ . The map $f$ is an injection by Lemma 2.4.8. Let $T^{\prime}$ denote a proper closed subgroup of $T$ of codimension $1$ , and let $U^{\prime}\subseteq T^{\prime}_{\beta}$ denote the complement of the union of the closed varieties $T^{\prime\prime}_{\beta}$ ranging over the proper closed subgroups $T^{\prime\prime}\subseteq T^{\prime}$ . By Lemma 2.4.6, the map $f$ is an isomorphism upon restriction to $U^{\prime}\subseteq T^{\prime}_{\beta}\subseteq T_{\beta}$ for each proper closed subgroup $T^{\prime}\subseteq T$ of codimension $1$ .

Therefore, the locus $Z\subseteq T_{\beta}$ over which $f$ fails to be an isomorphism is contained in the union of closed subvarieties $T^{\prime}_{\beta}$ for finitely many $T^{\prime}\subseteq T$ of codimension at least $2$ . However, the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)|_{T_{\beta}-Z}$ is an isomorphism (by Hartogs). Since the same is true of the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})|_{T_{\beta}-Z}$ , and the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})$ factors through the map $\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{(1)})\to\mathcal{F}_{T}(X^{T})$ , the desired result follows.

For the equalizer diagram, an easy induction on the cell structure of $X$ reduces us to the case $X=S^{\lambda}$ for a character $\lambda:T\to S^{1}$ . In this case, the isomorphism $T/T_{\lambda}\cong S^{\lambda}$ defines an isomorphism $\mathrm{ku}_{T_{\lambda}}\cong\mathcal{F}_{T}(S(\lambda))$ . Since $S^{\lambda}\cong\Sigma S(\lambda)$ , we obtain an equalizer diagram

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}(S^{\lambda})\to\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}\oplus\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}\cong\mathrm{Map}(\{0,\infty\},\mathrm{ku}_{T})\rightrightarrows\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T_{\lambda}}. $$

This proves the desired claim. ∎

#### Remark 2.4.11.

Note that the statement of Proposition 2.4.10 is natural in $X$ , and in particular, one can use Proposition 2.4.10 to describe the $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ -algebra structure on $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)$ . By dualizing Proposition 2.4.10, one can also describe the $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T}$ -coalgebra structure on $\mathrm{ku}^{T}_{\ast}(X)$ . Moreover, suppose that $X$ is a $T$ -space equipped with a presentation $X=\colim_{j\in\mathcal{J}}X_{j}$ in terms of finite $T$ -spaces, each of which is GKM and equipped with a chosen presentation in terms of $T$ -cells, and such that the transition maps $X_{j}\to X_{j^{\prime}}$ are maps of cellular $T$ -spaces. Then Proposition 2.4.10 can be extended to compute $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T}(X)$ and $\mathrm{ku}^{T}_{\ast}(X)$ .

## 3. (Derived) geometric Satake and variants

### 3.1. Full faithfulness of global sections

In this section, we prove an analogue of a result of Ginzburg’s from [Gin1]. We will closely follow [CMNO, Section 4.7] and [SW, Section 8].

#### Setup 3.1.1.

Let $G$ be a compact Lie group, and fix a maximal torus $T\subseteq G$ . Let $X$ be a finite $G$ -space whose $G$ -equivariant orbit stratification indexed by a poset $P$ (neccessarily finite). Let $X_{\lambda}$ denote the stratum corresponding to $\lambda\in P$ , and let $X_{\leq\lambda}$ denote its closure in $X$ . Suppose further that each $X_{\lambda}$ is a complex affine space of complex dimension $n_{\lambda}$ on which $G$ acts linearly. In particular, this implies that $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,!}\underline{\mathbf{Q}})$ is concentrated in even degrees for each $\lambda\in P$ , where $j_{\lambda}:X_{\lambda}\hookrightarrow X_{\leq\lambda}$ denotes the inclusion.

Let $X_{<\lambda}=X_{\leq\lambda}-X_{\lambda}$ , and let $i_{\lambda}:X_{<\lambda}\hookrightarrow X_{\leq\lambda}$ denote the complementary closed embedding. We will also write $j_{\lambda}$ to denote the inclusion $X_{\lambda}\hookrightarrow X$ . Let $\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ denote the $\infty$ -category of $G$ -equivariant sheaves on $X$ which are constructible for the $G$ -equivariant orbit stratification of $X$ . Recall that the cohomology functor $\Gamma:\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}$ is given by $\ast$ -pushforward to a point and then taking $G$ -homotopy fixed points of the resulting $\mathbf{Q}$ -module with $G$ -action.

#### Definition 3.1.2.

Let $\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ . Say that $\mathcal{F}$ is $\ast$ -even if the $\ast$ -pullback $j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})$ is a direct sum of constant sheaves concentrated in even degrees for all $\lambda\in P$ . Similarly, say that $\mathcal{F}$ is $!$ -even if the $!$ -pullback $j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})$ is a direct sum of constant sheaves concentrated in even degrees for all $\lambda\in P$ . Say that $\mathcal{F}$ is even if it is both $\ast$ -even and $!$ -even. Finally, say that $\mathcal{F}$ is ( $!$ - or $\ast$ -)odd if $\mathcal{F}[1]$ is ( $!$ - or $\ast$ -)even.

The goal of this section is to prove the following result, by inducting on the stratification of $X$ :

#### Theorem 3.1.3.

Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be even objects of $\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ . Then the map

$$ \Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\to\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{G})) $$

of graded $\mathbf{Q}$ -vector spaces is a graded isomorphism (the grading denoted by $\bullet$ ), where the $\Hom$ on the right-hand side is taken in the $1$ -category of graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ -modules in $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}^{\heartsuit}$ .

#### Remark 3.1.4.

Although Theorem 3.1.3 is stated only for $X$ being a finite $G$ -space, it can be extended easily to the situation when $X$ is not necessarily finite. Namely, suppose that $X$ is a $G$ -space equipped with a presentation $X=\colim_{j\in\mathcal{J}}X_{j}$ in terms of finite $G$ -spaces where each map $X_{j}\to X_{j^{\prime}}$ is a closed embedding. In this case, we will write $\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ to denote the inverse limit $\lim_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X_{j};\mathbf{Q})$ taken over $!$ -pullbacks; and the meaning of evenness is exactly as in Definition 3.1.2. With this definition of $\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ , Theorem 3.1.3 continues to hold verbatim.

#### Remark 3.1.5.

The argument for Theorem 3.1.3 below is sufficiently general that if $A$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring with homotopy concentrated in even degrees, given a good theory of $G$ -equivariant constructible sheaves of $A$ -modules on a stratified (finite) $G$ -space (including a six functor formalism), Theorem 3.1.3 will continue to hold as long as $\pi_{\ast}A_{G}$ is concentrated in even degrees. In particular, it continues to hold if $A=\mathbf{F}_{2}$ . However, we will only describe the argument for Theorem 3.1.3 with coefficients in $\mathbf{Q}$ .

#### Lemma 3.1.6.

Let $R$ be an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring, and let $M_{1}\to M_{2}\to M_{3}$ be a cofiber sequence of $R$ -modules such that each of $M_{1}$ , $M_{2}$ , and $M_{3}$ have homotopy concentrated in even degrees. Then there is a short exact sequence of graded $\pi_{\ast}R$ -modules

$$ 0\to\pi_{\ast}M_{1}\to\pi_{\ast}M_{2}\to\pi_{\ast}M_{3}\to 0. $$

#### Lemma 3.1.7.

Let $F:\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}$ be an exact functor. Then $F$ sends $\ast$ -even sheaves to $\mathbf{Q}$ -modules with even homotopy groups if and only if $F(j_{\lambda,!}\underline{\mathbf{Q}})$ has even homotopy groups for each $\lambda\in P$ .

#### Proof.

Suppose that $F$ sends $\ast$ -even sheaves to a $\mathbf{Q}$ -module with even homotopy groups. We claim that $F(j_{\lambda,!}\underline{\mathbf{Q}})$ has even homotopy groups for each $\lambda\in P$ : for this, it suffices to show that for each $\lambda^{\prime}\in\Lambda$ , the pullback $j_{\lambda^{\prime}}^{\ast}j_{\lambda,!}\underline{\mathbf{Q}}$ is a direct sum of constant sheaves concentrated in even degrees. But this is clear, because this pullback is zero unless $\lambda^{\prime}=\lambda$ , in which case it is just $\underline{\mathbf{Q}}$ .

Let us now show the other direction. Let $\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ be an $\ast$ -even sheaf, and fix $\lambda\in P$ such that $X_{\lambda}$ is contained in the support of $\mathcal{F}$ . Then there is a recollement

$$ j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}\to\mathcal{F}\to i_{\lambda,\ast}i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}. $$

Since $j_{\lambda}:X_{\lambda}\hookrightarrow X$ is open, we can identify $j_{\lambda}^{!}=j_{\lambda}^{\ast}$ , and so $j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}$ is a direct sum of constant sheaves concentrated in even degrees by assumption on $\mathcal{F}$ . This implies that $j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}$ is $\ast$ -even (by the argument in the preceding paragraph), so that $F(j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F})$ has even homotopy groups by our assumption on $F$ . Similarly, by induction on the strata contained in the support of $\mathcal{F}$ , we may assume that $F(i_{\lambda,\ast}i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})$ has even homotopy groups. Since $F(\mathcal{F})$ is an extension of $F(i_{\lambda,\ast}i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})$ by $F(j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F})$ , this implies that $F(\mathcal{F})$ also has even homotopy groups. ∎

#### Lemma 3.1.8.

The functor $\Gamma:\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}$ sends $\ast$ -even sheaves to $\mathbf{Q}$ -modules with even homotopy groups.

#### Proof.

By Lemma 3.1.7, we need to show that if $\lambda\in\Lambda$ , the global sections $\Gamma_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,!}\underline{\mathbf{Q}})$ has homotopy concentrated in even degrees. This is true by our assumption on $X_{\lambda}$ . ∎

#### Lemma 3.1.9.

Let $\mathcal{G}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ be $!$ -even. Then the functor $\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})\to\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}$ given by $\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(-,\mathcal{G})$ sends $\ast$ -even sheaves to $\mathbf{Q}$ -modules with even homotopy groups.

#### Proof.

By Lemma 3.1.7, we need to show that if $\lambda\in\Lambda$ , the $\mathbf{Q}$ -module $\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(j_{\lambda,!}\underline{\mathbf{Q}},\mathcal{G})$ has even homotopy. This $\mathbf{Q}$ -module can be identified with $\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})}(\underline{\mathbf{Q}},j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G})=\Gamma_{G}(X_{\lambda};j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G})$ . Since $j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G}$ is a direct sum of constant sheaves concentrated in even degrees (by assumption on $\mathcal{G}$ ), the desired result again follows from the assumption that $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})$ is concentrated in even degrees. ∎

#### Lemma 3.1.10.

Let $\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ be $\ast$ -even, and let $\mathcal{G}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ be $!$ -even. Then for each $\lambda\in P$ such that $X_{\lambda}$ is open in the support of $\mathcal{F}$ , there is an exact sequence

$$ 0\to\Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X_{<\lambda};\mathbf{Q})}(i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F},i_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F})\to\Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\to\Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})}(j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F},j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{G})\to 0. $$

#### Proof.

Recall that there is a recollement cofiber sequence

$$ j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}\to\mathcal{F}\to i_{\lambda,\ast}i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}. $$

Applying $\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(-,\mathcal{G})$ produces a cofiber sequence of $\mathbf{Q}$ -modules

$$ \mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(i_{\lambda,\ast}i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\to\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\to\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}). $$

Observe that $i_{\lambda,\ast}i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}$ and $j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}$ are both $\ast$ -even, so that Lemma 3.1.9 implies that each term in 3.1 has even homotopy. In particular, Lemma 3.1.6 implies that 3.1 induces a split exact sequence on homotopy groups. Note that by adjunction, we can rewrite the first term of 3.1 as $\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X_{<\lambda};\mathbf{Q})}(i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F},i_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G})$ , and the final term of 3.1 as $\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})}(j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F},j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{G})$ . Together with the above discussion, this proves the desired claim. ∎

#### Lemma 3.1.11.

Let $\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ be $\ast$ -even, and let $\mathcal{G}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ be $!$ -even. Then for each $\lambda\in P$ such that $X_{\lambda}$ is open in the support of $\mathcal{F}$ , there are exact sequences of graded $\mathbf{Q}$ -vector spaces

$$ \displaystyle 0\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}) \displaystyle\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})\to 0, \displaystyle 0\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G}) \displaystyle\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{G})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{\lambda};j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{G})\to 0. $$

#### Proof.

We will only prove the first exact sequence; the second follows by an entirely analogous argument. Again, recall that there is a recollement cofiber sequence

$$ j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}\to\mathcal{F}\to i_{\lambda,\ast}i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}. $$

Applying $\Gamma_{G}(X;-)$ gives a cofiber sequence

$$ \Gamma_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F})\to\Gamma_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})\to\Gamma_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}). $$

Observe that $i_{\lambda,\ast}i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}$ and $j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}$ are both $\ast$ -even, so that Lemma 3.1.8 implies that each term in this cofiber sequence has even homotopy. In particular, Lemma 3.1.6 implies that this cofiber sequence induces a split exact sequence on homotopy groups, as desired. ∎

#### Lemma 3.1.12.

Let $V$ be a complex affine space on which $G$ acts linearly, and equip $V$ with the trivial stratification. Then:

- (a) The functor $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;-):\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\xrightarrow{{\sim}}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{H}_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{Sp})$ is an equivalence, where the right-hand side denotes the $\infty$ -category of $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ -modules in spectra (i.e., the derived $\infty$ -category of chain complexes of $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ -modules). Moreover, if $\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ are sheaves such that $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathcal{F})$ is a projective $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ -module, there is a graded isomorphism

$$ \Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(V;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\xrightarrow{{\sim}}\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathcal{F}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathcal{G})). $$

Here, the $\Hom$ on the right-hand side is taken in the $1$ -category of graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ -modules in $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}^{\heartsuit}$ .

- (b) The compactly supported equivariant cohomology $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G,c}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ is isomorphic to a free $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -module generated by a single class $[V]$ in degree $\dim_{\mathbf{R}}(V)$ .

#### Proof.

Let us first show (a). Since $V$ is equipped with the trivial stratification, $\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ is equivalent to the $\infty$ -category of $G$ -equivariant local systems on $V$ . Because $V$ is a complex affine space, this is simply equivalent to the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ of $G$ -equivariant local systems of $\mathbf{Q}$ -modules on a point. Almost by definition, there is an equivalence $\mathrm{Loc}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_{C_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{Sp})$ . Since $G$ is assumed to be a compact Lie group, the $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebra $\pi_{\ast}C_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})=\mathrm{H}_{G}^{-\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ is isomorphic to a graded polynomial $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebra on generators in even negative (homological) degrees. Since the free ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebra on a generator $x$ in even degree is isomorphic to the polynomial algebra $\mathbf{Q}[x]$ , choosing polynomial generators for $\pi_{\ast}C_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ defines an equivalence $\mathrm{H}_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\cong C_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ of ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebras. It follows that there is an equivalence $\mathrm{Loc}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{H}_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{Sp})$ . Finally, if $\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ are sheaves such that $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathcal{F})$ is a projective graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ -module, the spectral sequence

$$ E_{2}=\Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathcal{F}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathcal{G}))\Rightarrow\pi_{-\ast}\Hom_{\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{H}_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{Sp})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathcal{F}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathcal{G})) $$

degenerates at the $E_{2}$ -page, where $\Ext^{\bullet}$ denotes the graded $\Ext$ -groups taken internal to the $1$ -category of graded $\mathrm{H}_{G}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -modules in $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}^{\heartsuit}$ . In fact, the $E_{2}$ -page is concentrated entirely in the zero line, since $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathcal{F})$ is a projective graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathbf{Q})$ -module (so there are no higher $\Ext$ -groups). In particular, we have

$$ \Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(V;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\xrightarrow{{\sim}}\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathcal{F}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(V;\mathcal{G})), $$

as desired.

Part (b) is simply the statement of (equivariant) Poincaré duality on an affine space. ∎

#### Remark 3.1.13.

It is natural to ask whether the statement of Lemma 3.1.12(a) is true for arbitrary $\mathcal{F}$ . Unfortunately, this need not be true. For example, suppose that $G=S^{1}$ , and that $V$ is the trivial vector space (without loss of generality). Using the equivalence $\mathrm{Loc}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\xrightarrow{{\sim}}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{Sp})$ and the fact that $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})=\mathbf{Q}[x]$ with $x$ in $\mathrm{H}^{2}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ , one can define an $S^{1}$ -local system on the point by the $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -module $\mathbf{Q}[x]/x=\mathbf{Q}$ . The extension class

$$ \mathbf{Q}[-2]\to\mathbf{Q}[x]/x^{2}\to\mathbf{Q} $$

defines a nontrivial element $\delta\in\pi_{1}\Hom_{\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{Sp})}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{Q})$ . However, this class cannot be seen from the graded $\Hom$ group: indeed,

$$ \Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}_{S^{1}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{Q})=\mathbf{Q} $$

in weight zero, generated by multiples of the identity map. The spectral sequence 3.2 still degenerates at the $E_{2}$ -page in this case, but there is a nontrivial class in $\Ext^{1}_{\mathrm{H}_{S^{1}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{Q})$ which detects the class $\delta$ .

The above example is intended to illustrate the difference between the $\infty$ -category of $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -modules in spectra, which can be identified with the derived $\infty$ -category of chain complexes of $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -modules, and the category of graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{S^{1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -modules in $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}^{\heartsuit}$ .

#### Lemma 3.1.15.

Let $\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ be $\ast$ -even, and let $\mathcal{G}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G}^{c}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ be $!$ -even. Suppose that the map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{\lambda};j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})$ is surjective for every $\lambda\in P$ , and that the map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{\lambda};j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{G})$ is injective for every $\lambda\in P$ . Then there is an exact sequence

$$ \displaystyle\hskip-28.45274pt0\to\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G}) \displaystyle\to\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{G})) \displaystyle\to\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{\lambda};j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{G})). $$

Here, the $\Hom$ s are taken in the $1$ -category of graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};\mathbf{Q})$ -modules (resp. $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ - and $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})$ -modules) in $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf{Q}}^{\heartsuit}$ .

Applied to $R=\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ and the exact sequences of Lemma 3.1.11, we see that the composite of Lemma 3.1.15 is exact on the left. For exactness in the middle, Lemma 3.1.15 says that we need to check:

- (a) Every graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ -linear map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G})$ factors through the map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})\twoheadrightarrow\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})$ .

The proof of (b) is entirely analogous to that of (a), so we will only show (a). Recall that $X_{\lambda}$ was assumed to be a complex affine space on which $G$ acts linearly. Therefore, the compactly supported equivariant cohomology $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G,c}(X_{\lambda};\mathbf{Q})$ is isomorphic to a free $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -module on a single generator (by Lemma 3.1.12(b)). Let us denote this generator by $[X_{\lambda}]$ .

Suppose we are given a graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ -linear map $f:\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G})$ . Then the following composite is zero

because $[X_{\lambda}]$ is zero in $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};\mathbf{Q})$ . Since $f$ is $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathbf{Q})$ -linear, this implies that the following composite is also zero:

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})[-2n_{\lambda}]\xrightarrow{{\cdot[X_{\lambda}]}}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})\xrightarrow{{f}}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{G}). $$

$$ \textstyle{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{<\lambda};i_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})/\im([X_{\lambda}]).} $$

By Poincaré duality on the affine space $X_{\lambda}$ , multiplication by $[X_{\lambda}]$ defines an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,\ast}j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})[-2n_{\lambda}]\xrightarrow{{\cdot[X_{\lambda}]}}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}). $$

$$ \textstyle{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})[-2n_{\lambda}]\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\cdot[X_{\lambda}]} \textstyle{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;\mathcal{F})} \textstyle{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X_{\lambda};j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\sim} \textstyle{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,\ast}j_{\lambda}^{\ast}\mathcal{F})[-2n_{\lambda}]\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\sim} \scriptstyle{\cdot[X_{\lambda}]} \textstyle{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(X;j_{\lambda,!}j_{\lambda}^{!}\mathcal{F}),\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} $$
