Therefore, 3.5 and Corollary 3.5.8 together make the following concrete prediction (see Remark 3.6.18 for an additional component of our prediction):

#### Conjecture 3.5.11.

On the spectral side of Conjecture 3.4.12, if ${\check{{M}}}$ is the Hamiltonian ${\check{{G}}}$ -space dual to $G/H$ , there is an isomorphism

$$ {\check{{M}}}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\cong{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}. $$

In general, if ${\check{{M}}}$ is the Hamiltonian ${\check{{G}}}$ -space which is dual to an affine (not necessarily homogeneous) spherical $G$ -variety, there is a “Kostant section” $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}}:{\check{{M}}}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\to{\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ which makes the following square commute:

$$ \textstyle{{\check{{M}}}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}}} \textstyle{{\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\mu} \textstyle{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\kappa} \textstyle{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{G}}}.} $$

Furthermore, $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}}$ can be refined (non-uniquely) to a map ${\check{{M}}}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\to{\check{{M}}}$ such that the algebra of regular functions on its ${\check{{G}}}$ -orbit is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{M}}}}$ .

Motivated by [Kno1, Kno2] (see Remark 3.3.15 for a brief summary), we further expect the following. Suppose that ${\check{{M}}}$ can be written as $T^{\ast}{\check{{X}}}$ for a spherical ${\check{{G}}}$ -variety ${\check{{X}}}$ , and let $\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{B}}}}({\check{{X}}})$ (resp. $\mathcal{O}_{B}(G/H)$ ) denote the poset of ${\check{{B}}}$ -orbit closures in ${\check{{X}}}$ (resp. $B$ -orbit closures in $G/H$ ) equipped with the Bruhat order. Then there is a bijection $\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{B}}}}({\check{{X}}})\leftrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{B}(G/H)$ which is equivariant for the action of the Weyl group $W_{{\check{{G}}}}\cong W_{G}$ on either side described in [Kno2].2121 21 Said differently, there is a $W$ -equivariant bijection between the sets of irreducible components of $T^{\ast}(G/H)\times_{\mathfrak{b}^{\ast}}\{0\}$ and ${\check{{M}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}}\{0\}$ , where $T^{\ast}(G/H)\to\mathfrak{b}^{\ast}$ (resp. ${\check{{M}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}$ ) is the moment map for the $B$ - (resp. ${\check{{B}}}$ -)action.

Under this bijection, the results of [Kno1, Kno2, Res] (see Remark 3.3.15 for a brief summary) should give an isomorphism between the stabilizers of a minimal rank $B$ -orbit on $G/H$ and of the closure ${\check{{X}}}$ of the open ${\check{{B}}}$ -orbit in ${\check{{X}}}$ ; in other words, there is an isomorphism

$$ W_{{\check{{X}}}}\ltimes W_{L(X)}\cong W_{H}. $$

If $\mathfrak{t}_{H}$ denotes a Cartan of $H$ and $\mathfrak{t}_{{\check{{X}}}}$ denotes the Cartan of ${\check{{X}}}$ , there should be a canonical $W_{L(X)}$ -Galois covering $\mathfrak{t}_{H}\to\mathfrak{t}_{{\check{{X}}}}^{\ast}$ which is equivariant for the surjection $W_{H}\twoheadrightarrow W_{{\check{{X}}}}$ .

Some brief comments regarding Conjecture 3.5.11:

- • Just as the Kostant slice plays a crucial role in the geometric Langlands program, we expect the Kostant section $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}}$ to play a central role in the story of relative geometric Langlands.

- • Since ${\check{{M}}}=\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}}(S_{X}\oplus({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}_{X}^{\perp}\cap{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{e}))$ by Lemma 3.4.6, the first part of Conjecture 3.5.11 is equivalent to the statement that

$$ (S_{X}\oplus({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}_{X}^{\perp}\cap{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{e}))/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}_{X}\cong{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}. $$

The latter being a polynomial ring (by Chevalley restriction and Chevalley-Shephard-Todd), we see that Conjecture 3.5.11 forces in particular that the action of ${\check{{G}}}_{X}$ on $S_{X}\oplus({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}_{X}^{\perp}\cap{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{e})$ be coregular.

- • The penultimate paragraph of Conjecture 3.5.11 clearly generalizes to the case when $T^{\ast}(G/H)$ is replaced by a more general Hamiltonian $G$ -space. In fact, this generalization of the penultimate part of Conjecture 3.5.11 appears as [FGT, Conjecture 1.1.1]; I am grateful to Akshay Venkatesh and Zhiwei Yun for informing me of this paper.

- • The middle part of Conjecture 3.5.11 should be a starting point for proving Conjecture 3.4.14.

- • The final paragraph of Conjecture 3.5.11 attempts to provide a “geometric reason” for the expected isomorphism $(T^{\ast}{\check{{X}}})/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\cong\mathfrak{t}_{H}/\!\!/W_{H}$ : indeed, as described in Remark 3.3.15, Knop has shown that $(T^{\ast}{\check{{X}}})/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\cong\mathfrak{t}_{{\check{{X}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/W_{{\check{{X}}}}$ , and the final part of Conjecture 3.5.11 identifies this with $\mathfrak{t}_{H}/\!\!/W_{H}$ .

#### Corollary 3.5.12.

The ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ -algebra structure obtained via the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -map $\mathrm{ku}_{G}\to\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ on the $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))$ – which is not $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))^{\vee}$ in the notation of Construction 2.4.4 – refines to an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ -algebra structure.

#### Proof.

Taking the $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -linear dual of the right-hand side of Proposition 3.5.7 produces the Hochschild cohomology $\mathrm{HC}(\mathrm{ku}_{H}/\mathrm{ku}_{G})$ . By the Deligne conjecture (in the form proved in [Lur3, Section 5.3]), this admits the structure of an ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ -algebra. On the other hand, by Proposition 3.5.1, the right-hand side of Proposition 3.5.7 can be identified with the equivariant cohomology $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))$ . The desired result follows. ∎

#### Remark 3.5.13.

One can also identify the $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega G)$ with the ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -centralizer of the map $\mathrm{ku}_{G}\to\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ ; see Recollection 5.2.4. The ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -structure on the $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))$ is essentially the reason for the ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -monoidal structure on the relative Langlands category $\mathrm{Shv}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})$ (to be defined below) from [BZSV, Remark 7.5.12 and Section 16].

In the special case when $G=H\times H$ and $H$ is embedded diagonally, one can identify $\mathrm{HC}(\mathrm{ku}_{H}/\mathrm{ku}_{G})$ with the ${\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}$ -Hochschild cohomology $\mathrm{HC}_{\mathbf{E}_{{2}}}(\mathrm{ku}_{H}/\mathrm{ku})$ . The Deligne conjecture therefore equips the $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega H)$ with an ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ -algebra structure, and again this is essentially the source of the folklore ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ -monoidal structure on the spherical Hecke category $\mathrm{Shv}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}_{H[\![t]\!]\times H[\![t]\!]}(H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})$ . We will use the perspective of ${\mathbf{E}_{{n}}}$ -centers to establish some coisotropicity results in Section 5.2.

#### Warning 3.5.14.

The reader should keep Warning 3.5.5 in mind: the $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))$ is not equivalent to the $\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!))$ . In fact, as mentioned in Corollary 3.5.12, the $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))$ is also not equivalent to the equivariant homology $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))^{\vee}$ ; the former is only a completion of the latter.

#### Remark 3.5.15.

There are, of course, many mild variants of Corollary 3.5.12. For instance, suppose $K\subseteq H$ is a closed subgroup. Then $\mathrm{ku}_{K}$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -algebra; in particular, it is a $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -bimodule in $\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ -modules. Therefore, one can consider the Hochschild cohomology $\mathrm{HC}(\mathrm{ku}_{H}/\mathrm{ku}_{G};\mathrm{ku}_{K})$ with coefficients in the bimodule $\mathrm{ku}_{K}$ . Just as in Corollary 3.5.12, one can identify $\mathrm{HC}(\mathrm{ku}_{H}/\mathrm{ku}_{G};\mathrm{ku}_{K})$ with the $\mathrm{ku}_{K}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{K}(\Omega(G/H))$ . It follows, for instance, that $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(C^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})/C^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z});C^{\ast}_{K}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}))$ is a completion of $\mathrm{H}^{K}_{\ast}(\Omega(G/H);\mathbf{Z})$ .

#### Example 3.5.16.

Let us illustrate Corollary 3.5.12, or rather, the identification of the $\mathrm{ku}_{H}$ -linear dual of $\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))$ with Hochschild cohomology, after base-changing along the map $\mathrm{ku}_{H}\to\mathrm{ku}\to\mathbf{Z}$ (to $\mathbf{Z}[1/2]$ in the second example) in two simple cases:

- (a) Let $H=\mathrm{SU}(n-1)\subseteq\mathrm{SU}(n)=G$ . Then $G/H\simeq S^{2n-1}$ , and so there is an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}_{H}}\mathbf{Z}\cong\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n-1};\mathbf{Z})\cong\mathbf{Z}[y], $$

where $y$ lives in weight $2n-2$ . On the other hand, the map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})$ identifies with the map

$$ \mathbf{Z}[c_{1},\cdots,c_{n}]\to\mathbf{Z}[c_{1},\cdots,c_{n-1}] $$

sending $c_{n}\mapsto 0$ , where the $i$ th Chern class $c_{i}$ lives in weight $-2i$ . Taking Hochschild homology along this map identifies

$$ \mathrm{HH}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})/\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}))\simeq\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}\mathrm{HH}(\mathbf{Z}/\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathbf{Z}[c_{n}]). $$

But $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HH}(\mathbf{Z}/\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathbf{Z}[c_{n}])$ is isomorphic to the divided power algebra $\mathbf{Z}\langle{\sigma^{2}(c_{n})}\rangle$ , where $\sigma$ denotes “suspension”, so that $\sigma^{2}(c_{n})$ lives in degree $-2n+2$ ; it follows that there is an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HH}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})/\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}))\cong\mathbf{Z}[c_{1},\cdots,c_{n-1}]\langle{\sigma^{2}(c_{n})}\rangle. $$

This in turn implies that there is an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})/\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}))\cong\mathbf{Z}[c_{1},\cdots,c_{n-1}][\![y]\!] $$

where the class $y$ in weight $2n-2$ is dual to $\sigma^{2}(c_{n})$ . Killing $c_{1},\cdots,c_{n}$ (i.e., base-changing along $\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})\to\mathbf{Z}$ ) precisely recovers a completion of $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n-1};\mathbf{Z})$ . We will discuss a generalization (and decompletion) of this calculation in Theorem 4.2.13.

- (b) Let $H=\mathrm{SO}_{2n}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}=G$ with $n>0$ , and recall that we are replacing $\mathbf{Z}$ by $\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}=\mathbf{Z}[1/2]$ . Then $G/H\simeq S^{2n}$ , and so a standard argument with the Serre spectral sequence shows that there is an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{H}(\Omega(G/H))^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}_{H}}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}\cong\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[y,z]/z^{2}, $$

where $z$ lives in weight $2n-1$ and $y$ lives in weight $4n-2$ . On the other hand, the map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ identifies with the map

$$ \mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},p_{n}]\to\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},p_{n}^{1/2}] $$

sending $p_{n}\mapsto(p_{n}^{1/2})^{2}$ , where the $i$ th Pontryagin class $p_{i}$ lives in weight $-4i$ and the Euler class $p_{n}^{1/2}$ lives in weight $-2n$ . Taking Hochschild homology along this map identifies

$$ \mathrm{HH}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})/\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}))\simeq\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1}]\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}}\mathrm{HH}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{n}^{1/2}]/\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{n}]), $$

and so computing the Hochschild cohomology from Corollary 3.5.12 amounts to computing the Hochschild cohomology $\mathrm{HC}(\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{n}^{1/2}]/\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{n}])$ . Lemma 3.5.17 implies that there is an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})/\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}))\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},p_{n}^{1/2}][\![w]\!]/p_{n}^{1/2}w, $$

with $w$ in in weight $4n-2$ . Upon killing $p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},p_{n}^{1/2}$ (i.e., base-changing along $\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})\to\mathbf{Z}$ ), one precisely recovers a completion of $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ . We will discuss a generalization (and decompletion) of this calculation in Theorem 4.2.13.

#### Lemma 3.5.17.

Let $x$ be a class in homological degree $2n$ , and let $j\geq 1$ . Then there is an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\mathbf{Z}[x]/\mathbf{Z}[x^{j}])\cong\mathbf{Z}[x][\![w]\!]/jx^{j-1}w, $$

where $w$ lives in weight $-2nj-2$ .

#### Proof.

Since $\mathbf{Z}[x]=\mathrm{sh}\mathbf{Z}[x_{n}]$ where $x_{n}$ lives in weight $n$ and degree $0$ , it suffices to work in the graded setting and assume that $x$ lives in weight $n$ and degree $0$ . Let us first work in the ungraded setting; fix a nonconstant polynomial $g(x)\in\mathbf{Z}[x]$ , and consider $\mathrm{HC}(\mathbf{Z}[x]/\mathbf{Z}[g])$ . There is an isomorphism

$$ \mathbf{Z}[x]\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}[g]}\mathbf{Z}[x]\cong\mathbf{Z}[x,x^{\prime}]/(g(x)-g(x^{\prime}))\cong\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf, $$

where $z=x^{\prime}-x$ and $f=\frac{g(x)-g(x+z)}{z}$ . (If $x$ has weight $n$ and $g$ is homogeneous of degree $j$ , the class $z$ lives in degree $0$ and weight $n$ , and $f$ lives in degree $0$ and weight $n(j-1)$ .) Our goal is to compute $\pi_{\ast}\End_{\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf}(\mathbf{Z}[x])$ , where the map $\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf\to\mathbf{Z}[x]$ sends $z\mapsto 0$ . There are several ways to compute this: one is to note that there is a presentation

$$ \mathbf{Z}[x]\simeq(\mathbf{Z}[x,z,u]\langle{v}\rangle/(zf,u^{2}),d(u)=z,d(v)=uf) $$

of $\mathbf{Z}[x]$ as a $\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf$ -algebra. If $x$ has weight $n$ and $g$ is homogeneous of degree $j$ , the class $u$ is in degree $1$ and weight $n$ , and $v$ is a divided power class in degree $2$ and weight $nj$ . This implies that there is an equivalence

$$ \End_{\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf}(\mathbf{Z}[x])\simeq(\mathbf{Z}[x,u^{\prime}][\![w]\!]/{u^{\prime}}^{2},d(u^{\prime})=f(z=0)w), $$

where $u^{\prime}$ is dual to $u$ and $w$ is dual to $v$ . If $x$ has weight $n$ and $g$ is homogeneous of degree $j$ , the class $u^{\prime}$ is in degree $-1$ and weight $-n$ , and $w$ is in degree $-2$ and weight $-nj$ . It follows that there is a class $w\in\pi_{-2}\End_{\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf}(\mathbf{Z}[x])$ such that $f(z=0)w=0\in\pi_{-2}\End_{\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf}(\mathbf{Z}[x])$ , which gives an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\mathbf{Z}[x]/\mathbf{Z}[g])=\pi_{\ast}\End_{\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf}(\mathbf{Z}[x])\cong\mathbf{Z}[x][\![w]\!]/g^{\prime}(0)w. $$

If $x$ has weight $n$ and $g$ is homogeneous of degree $j$ , the class $w$ lives in $\pi_{-2,-nj}\End_{\mathbf{Z}[x,z]/zf}(\mathbf{Z}[x])$ , and we obtain a graded isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\mathbf{Z}[x]/\mathbf{Z}[x^{j}])\cong\mathbf{Z}[x][\![w]\!]/jx^{j-1}w, $$

which gives the desired calculation by shearing. ∎

#### Remark 3.5.18.

As in Lemma 3.5.17, one can also compute $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}/\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{SU}(2)})$ to obtain the following:

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}/\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{SU}(2)})\cong\mathbf{Z}[\beta,x,\tfrac{1}{1+\beta x}][\![w]\!]/w(x-\overline{x}). $$

Here, $w$ lives in degree $0$ and weight $2$ , and $\overline{x}=-\frac{x}{1+\beta x}$ is the negative of $x$ under the group law on $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}=\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}$ . When $\beta=0$ , this recovers Lemma 3.5.17 for $j=2$ and $n=-1$ . There is a spectral sequence whose $E_{1}$ -page is $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}/\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{SU}(2)})$ which converges to $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}/\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{SU}(2)})$ ; this spectral sequence degenerates. Since the $2$ -series of $x$ is $[2](x)=(1+\beta x)(x-\overline{x})$ , we find that

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\mathrm{ku}_{S^{1}}/\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{SU}(2)})\cong\mathbf{Z}[\beta,x,\tfrac{1}{1+\beta x}][\![w]\!]/w[2](x), $$

where $w$ lives in degree $2$ .

#### Remark 3.5.19.

The reader might observe that one can analyze $\mathrm{HH}(\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{H}/\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{G})$ essentially using the combinatorics of the weight lattices and Weyl groups of $H$ and $G$ . More generally, therefore, let $W_{1}\to W_{2}$ be a homomorphism of finite groups acting on vector spaces $V_{1}\to V_{2}$ over a field $k$ (possibly of nonzero characteristic). Then there is a map $V_{1}/\!\!/W_{1}\to V_{2}/\!\!/W_{2}$ , and hence one can consider the Hochschild homology $\mathrm{HH}(V_{1}/\!\!/W_{1}/V_{2}/\!\!/W_{2})$ . This should be an interesting invariant associated to homomorphisms of finite groups, but it is likely only well-behaved if the map $V_{1}/\!\!/W_{1}\to V_{2}/\!\!/W_{2}$ is an affine bundle.

For instance, Proposition 3.5.7 and Example 3.6.13 below imply that the Hochschild cohomology $\mathrm{HC}(\mathfrak{t}/\mathfrak{t}/\!\!/W)$ is closely related to a completion of the “regular centralizer” ${\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\times_{{\check{{G}}}\backslash\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}}{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}$ for $\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}$ . More generally, if $\mathfrak{g}$ is a simple Lie algebra (over $\mathbf{C}$ ) with Weyl group $W$ and Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{t}$ , $V$ is a miniscule representation of $\mathfrak{g}$ , and $W_{H}$ is the stabilizer of a weight of $V$ , one obtains a Gelfand pair $(W,W_{H})$ . The combinatorial properties of this Gelfand pair “control” the Hochschild cohomology $\mathrm{HC}(\mathfrak{t}/\!\!/W_{H}/\mathfrak{t}/\!\!/W)$ . One therefore expects $\mathrm{HC}(\mathfrak{t}/\!\!/W_{H}/\mathfrak{t}/\!\!/W)$ to be an interesting combinatorial invariant of $V$ .

One example which does not come from Lie-theoretic data is the dihedral group $D_{2n}$ acting on $\mathbf{A}^{2}=\spec\mathbf{C}[x_{1},x_{2}]$ by the matrices $s=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\ 0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and $r=\begin{pmatrix}\zeta_{n}&0\\ 0&\zeta_{n}^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$ . The algebra of invariants $\mathbf{C}[x_{1},x_{2}]^{D_{2n}}$ is simply $\mathbf{C}[x_{1}x_{2},x_{1}^{n}+x_{2}^{n}]$ . As in Lemma 3.5.17, one finds that

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{HC}(\mathbf{A}^{2}/\mathbf{A}^{2}/\!\!/D_{2n})\cong\mathbf{C}[x_{1},x_{2}][\![w_{1},w_{2}]\!]/\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}&x_{2}\\
x_{2}^{n-1}&x_{1}^{n-1}\end{pmatrix}\vec{w}. $$

#### Example 3.5.20.

Consider the subgroup $G^{\mathrm{diag}}\subseteq G\times G$ , so that $(G\times G)/G^{\mathrm{diag}}\simeq G$ (this is the “group case” of Example 3.3.5). Then Proposition 3.5.7 says that there is an $S^{1}$ -equivariant equivalence of ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ -algebras

$$ \mathcal{F}_{G\times G}(\mathcal{L}G)\simeq\mathrm{HH}(\mathrm{ku}_{G}/\mathrm{ku}_{G\times G}). $$

By construction of equivariant $\mathrm{ku}$ , there is an equivalence $\mathrm{ku}_{G\times G}\simeq\mathrm{ku}_{G}\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}}\mathrm{ku}_{G}$ , so that the right-hand side can be identified with the factorization homology

$$ \mathrm{HH}(\mathrm{ku}_{G}/\mathrm{ku}_{G}\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}}\mathrm{ku}_{G})\simeq\int_{S^{2}}\mathrm{ku}_{G}/\mathrm{ku}. $$

Note that by Proposition 3.5.1, the left-hand side can be identified with $\mathcal{F}_{G}(\Omega G)$ , so Proposition 3.5.7 describes the $G$ -equivariant $\mathrm{ku}$ -cohomology of the affine Grassmannian:

$$ \mathrm{ku}^{\ast}_{G}(\Omega G)\simeq\pi_{\ast}\int_{S^{2}}\mathrm{ku}_{G}/\mathrm{ku}. $$

Note that there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{HH}(\mathrm{ku}_{G}/\mathrm{ku}_{G}\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}}\mathrm{ku}_{G})\simeq\mathrm{ku}_{G}\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}}\mathrm{HH}(\mathrm{ku}/\mathrm{ku}_{G}). $$

Upon killing the Bott class $\beta$ , 3.8 implies that

$$ C^{\ast}_{G}(\Omega G;\mathbf{Z})\simeq\int_{S^{2}}C^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Z})/\mathbf{Z}. $$

As argued in [Dev2, Example A.8], this recovers [BF1, Theorem 1] and [Gin2, Section 1.7] upon rationalization.

#### Remark 3.5.21.

Unlike Proposition 3.5.1, Proposition 3.5.7 gives an $S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}$ -equivariant equivalence. In particular, it allows us to calculate the $S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}$ -equivariant cohomology $\mathrm{ku}^{\ast}_{G\times G\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}(\mathcal{L}G)\simeq\mathrm{ku}^{\ast}_{G\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}(\Omega G)$ . We will discuss this in a future article, since addressing loop rotation in the detail it deserves will take us too far afield.

However, since it is not very difficult to make explicit, let us explicate Proposition 3.5.7 (or rather, its variant for Hochschild cohomology describing $\mathrm{ku}^{G\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\Omega G)$ ) in the case when $G=T$ is a torus. (At the beginning of this section, we asked that $G$ be simply-connected; this is obviously not true for a torus, but that assumption was necessary only when doing computations with Hochschild (co)homology. We will not use this perspective below.)

As in [Dev2, Proposition 3.3.4], the associative graded ring $\mathrm{ku}^{T\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\Omega T)$ can be identified with the algebra of $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ -differential operators on the dual torus ${\check{{T}}}$ . This is an analogue of the algebra of (asymptotic) differential operators. Let us assume for simplicity that $T$ is of rank $1$ ; then the algebra $\mathrm{ku}^{T\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\Omega T)$ is the $F$ -Weyl algebra $F\mathcal{D}_{\square,\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ of [DM2, Definition 4.4.1] for $F(x,y)=x+y+\beta xy$ , at least up to completion. Explicitly, when $T=S^{1}$ , we have

$$ \mathrm{ku}^{T\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\Omega T)\cong\mathbf{Z}[\beta,\hbar,\tfrac{1}{1+\beta\hbar}]\{x,a^{\pm 1}\}[\tfrac{1}{1+\beta x}]/([x,a]=a\hbar(1+\beta x)). $$

Here, the curly brackets denotes the free associative algebra generated by the elements enclosed within. The classes $\hbar$ and $x$ live in weight $-2$ (they are the $S^{1}$ -equivariant Chern classes for $\mathrm{ku}$ ), $\beta$ lives in weight $2$ , and $a$ lives in weight zero. Let us note two specializations of this associative algebra:

- (a) If $\beta=0$ , the right-hand side above simply becomes $\mathbf{Z}[\hbar]\{x,a^{\pm 1}\}/([x,a]=\hbar a)$ , which is precisely the algebra of asymptotic differential operators on ${\check{{T}}}=\spec\mathbf{Z}[a^{\pm 1}]$ over $\mathbf{Z}$ . Namely, $x=\hbar a\partial_{a}$ ; see [DM2, Example 4.4.2].

- (b) If $\beta$ is inverted, all elements can be pushed to degree zero. Namely, let $q=1+\beta\hbar$ and $\Theta=1+\beta x$ . Then there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\pm 1},\hbar,\tfrac{1}{1+\beta\hbar}]\{x,a^{\pm 1}\}[\tfrac{1}{1+\beta x}]/([x,a]-a\hbar(1+\beta x))\cong\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\pm 1},q^{\pm 1}]\{\Theta^{\pm 1},a^{\pm 1}\}/(\Theta a-qa\Theta), $$

since $\displaystyle\Theta a$ $\displaystyle=(1+\beta x)a=a+\beta xa=a+\beta a(x+\hbar+\beta\hbar x)$ $\displaystyle=a(1+\beta x)(1+\beta\hbar)=qa\Theta.$ In particular, $\mathrm{ku}^{T\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\Omega T)[1/\beta]=\mathrm{KU}^{T\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\Omega T)$ can be identified with the $q$ -Weyl algebra of ${\check{{T}}}=\spec\mathbf{Z}[a^{\pm 1}]$ . Namely, $\Theta=q^{a\partial_{a}}$ ; see [DM2, Example 4.4.3].

In general, $\mathrm{ku}^{T\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\Omega T)$ interpolates between the algebra of asymptotic differential and $q$ -difference operators on ${\check{{T}}}$ .

#### Remark 3.6.3.

Before proceeding to the argument, let us make one comment about Hypothesis 3.5.2: as the terminology suggests, a subgroup being optimal is a rather idealized situation; it is essentially the smallest set of hypotheses needed to make the argument of Theorem 3.2.7 go through. It is, of course, possible that examples of interest (even the ones considered in this article) do not satisfy this condition. Verifying Hypothesis 3.5.2 is likely no easy task, and working out the appropriate subtleties of the sheaf theories involved in Conjecture 3.4.12 will be very important to understanding microlocal aspects of relative geometric Langlands. $$ \Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}^{c}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{IC}_{0},\mathrm{IC}_{0}\star{\check{{\mathcal{R}}}})\\
\cong\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{IC}_{0}),\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{IC}_{0}\star{\check{{\mathcal{R}}}})). $$

There is an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{IC}_{0})\cong\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(G/H;\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}}, $$

and hence an isomorphism

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{IC}_{0}\star{\check{{\mathcal{R}}}}) \displaystyle\cong\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{IC}_{0})\otimes_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{(G\times G)[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{IC}_{0})}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{(G\times G)[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{IC}_{0}\star{\check{{\mathcal{R}}}}) \displaystyle\cong\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}}}\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)} \displaystyle\cong\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}\times{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}. $$

Moreover, there is an isomorphism $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\mathcal{L}(G/H);\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\Omega(G/H);\mathbf{Q})$ by Remark 3.5.4, so we find that there is a graded isomorphism

$$ \Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}^{c}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{IC}_{0},\mathrm{IC}_{0}\star{\check{{\mathcal{R}}}})\cong\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\Omega(G/H);\mathbf{Q})}(\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}},\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}\times{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)})\\
\cong\Hom^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}(\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}},\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}\times{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)})^{\spec\mathrm{H}^{H}_{\ast}(\Omega(G/H);\mathbf{Q})}\cong\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}\times{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}^{\spec\mathrm{H}^{H}_{\ast}(\Omega(G/H);\mathbf{Q})}. $$

By (b), there is an isomorphism $\spec\mathrm{H}^{H}_{\ast}(\Omega(G/H);\mathbf{Q})={\check{{J}}}_{X}\cong{\check{{J}}}_{X}^{\prime}$ , and hence there is an isomorphism

$$ \Ext^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Shv}^{c}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})}(\mathrm{IC}_{0},\mathrm{IC}_{0}\star{\check{{\mathcal{R}}}})\cong\mathcal{O}_{({\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}\times{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho))/{\check{{J}}}_{X}^{\prime}}. $$

By (a), this is further isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{M}}}}$ . Using 3.11, it follows that $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}$ is equivalent to the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Perf}_{\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{M}}}}}\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}({\check{{M}}}))$ . This in turn implies that $\mathcal{C}$ is equivalent to the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho))$ , as desired. ∎

#### Remark 3.6.5.

In this article, we will only focus on applying Theorem 3.6.4 to the case when $G_{\mathbf{C}}/H_{\mathbf{C}}$ is a spherical $G_{\mathbf{C}}$ -variety of rank $1$ . However, in [Dev4], we use Theorem 3.6.4 to study Conjecture 3.4.12 for the spherical subgroups $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}\subseteq\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ and $\mathrm{G}_{2}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{8}/\mu_{2}$ of relative rank $3$ . In [CMNO], Theorem 3.6.4 was used in the case when $G_{\mathbf{C}}/H_{\mathbf{C}}=\mathrm{GL}_{2n}/\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$ to show that the dual quotient stack ${\check{{M}}}/\mathrm{GL}_{2n}(-2\rho)$ identifies with $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}(4-4\rho)/\mathrm{GL}_{n}(-4\rho)$ . This relies on the following isomorphism of group schemes over $\spec\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n}(4)/\!\!/\Sigma_{n}$ :

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}}_{\ast}(\Omega(\mathrm{GL}_{2n}/\mathrm{Sp}_{2n});\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n}(4)/\!\!/\Sigma_{n}\times_{\mathfrak{gl}_{n}^{\ast}(4-4\rho)/\mathrm{GL}_{n}(-4\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{n}(4)/\!\!/\Sigma_{n}. $$

Here, the map $\mathfrak{t}^{n}(4)/\!\!/\Sigma_{n}\to\mathfrak{gl}_{n}^{\ast}(4-4\rho)/\mathrm{GL}_{n}(-4\rho)$ is given by the Kostant slice. However, more is true: 3.12 can be refined to an isomorphism

In future work, we will study some more exotic examples. #### Remark 3.6.7.

One can see Lemma 3.6.6 more directly as follows. Theorem 3.2.15 and Corollary 3.2.17 together imply that there is a homomorphism

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{G}_{\ast}(\Omega G;\mathbf{Q})\cong{\check{{J}}}\to{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)\times{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{G}}} $$

of graded group schemes over ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\cong\spec\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ . Base-changing along the map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{H}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ , we obtain a homomorphism

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{H}_{\ast}(\Omega G;\mathbf{Q})\to{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)\times{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}. $$

Composition with the map $\spec\mathrm{H}^{H}_{\ast}(\Omega(G/H);\mathbf{Q})\to\spec\mathrm{H}^{H}_{\ast}(\Omega G;\mathbf{Q})$ induced by the map $G\to G/H$ produces the desired homomorphism.

Note that this leads to the following description of ${\check{{M}}}$ (ignoring gradings for simplicity), which amounts to turning Theorem 3.6.4 on its head. Namely, recall that we defined ${\check{{J}}}_{X}=\spec\mathrm{H}^{H}_{\ast}(\Omega(G/H);\mathbf{Q})$ . Then, Lemma 3.6.6 gives a map $B_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}}{\check{{J}}}_{X}\to B_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}}({\check{{J}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}})$ of stacks over ${\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}$ . In particular, there is a canonical composite

$$ B_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}}{\check{{J}}}_{X}\to B_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{J}}}\cong{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}}\to B{\check{{G}}}. $$

One can then identify ${\check{{M}}}$ with the affine closure of $B_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}}{\check{{J}}}_{X}\times_{B{\check{{G}}}}\spec(\mathbf{Q})$ . Said differently, ${\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ can be thought of as the “affine closure of $B_{{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}}{\check{{J}}}_{X}$ relative to $B{\check{{G}}}$ ”.

Observe that one can define some scheme ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ in this way even if $G/H$ is not spherical (one just needs $H$ to be reductive; in fact, the below definition can be made for any homomorphism $H\to G$ )

$$ {{\check{{M}}}}^{\ddagger}=\overline{({\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}})/{\check{{J}}}_{X}}. $$

One generally has very little control of ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ if it is constructed via 3.14. However, one can at the very least use 3.18 to obtain a Lagrangian morphism ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{G}}}$ , which by Proposition 5.1.8 can be understood as equipping ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ with the structure of a Hamiltonian ${\check{{G}}}$ -space.

The definition of ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ is rigged so that if Hypothesis 3.5.2 is satisfied, there is an equivalence of categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)). $$

#### Notation.

We will write ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ to denote the scheme of 3.14, and when $H\subseteq G$ is spherical, we will write ${\check{{M}}}$ (without the ${\ddagger}$ ) to denote the scheme defined in [BZSV, Section 4]. The question of proving Conjecture 3.4.12 (when $H\subseteq G$ is spherical) becomes about identifying ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ with ${\check{{M}}}$ . In Section 4, we verify this for rank $1$ homogeneous spherical varieties by explicit calculation. In the general case, understanding Conjecture 3.6.8 should be an important step in this process.

The perspective on ${\check{{M}}}$ as being ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ (defined by 3.14) leads to several interesting and nontrivial structures. For instance, $G/H$ has an action of its $G$ -equivariant automorphism group $\mathrm{N}_{G}(H)/H$ , and hence $\mathrm{N}_{G}(H)/H$ acts on ${\check{{J}}}_{X}$ . The above construction of ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ therefore shows that there is a natural $\mathrm{N}_{G}(H)/H$ -action on ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ , and hence an expected $\mathrm{N}_{G}(H)/H$ -action on ${\check{{M}}}$ , which commutes with its Hamiltonian ${\check{{G}}}$ -action. This action is highly interesting; for instance, when $H=T\subseteq G$ , we check in Example 3.6.13 that ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}$ is the affine closure of $T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})$ ; the above action of $\mathrm{N}_{G}(T)/T\cong W$ turns out to be Gelfand-Graev action of the Weyl group on $\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}$ (as described by Ginzburg-Kazhdan in [GK]).

#### Example 3.6.13.

For simplicity, we will ignore gradings in the following discussion. Let $G_{\mathbf{C}}$ be an almost simple algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ , and let $T_{\mathbf{C}}\subseteq G_{\mathbf{C}}$ be a maximal torus. Note that $(G_{\mathbf{C}}\times T_{\mathbf{C}})/T_{\mathbf{C}}^{\mathrm{diag}}\cong G_{\mathbf{C}}$ is generally not a spherical $G_{\mathbf{C}}\times T_{\mathbf{C}}$ -variety (just for dimension reasons). Nevertheless, one expects that there is a $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}_{(G\times T)[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}/({\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{T}}})) $$

which is equivariant for the left-action of $\mathrm{Shv}_{(G\times T)[\![t]\!]\times(G\times T)[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}((G\times T)(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2-2\rho)/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)\times{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}[2]/{\check{{T}}})$ via Theorem 3.2.7. Note that 3.16 implies that there is a $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/T(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}/{\check{{G}}}). $$

Moreover, were the equivalence 3.16 true, the canonical action of the Weyl group $W=N_{G}(T)/T$ on the left-hand side of 3.16 should correspond to the ${\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{T}}}$ -equivariant (semi-classical) Gelfand-Graev action on $\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}$ as studied in [GK]. For the case when $G$ has semisimple rank $1$ , see Corollary 4.3.19 and Remark 4.3.20. When $G=\mathrm{PGL}_{3}$ , the affine closure $\overline{T^{\ast}(\mathrm{SL}_{3}/{\check{{N}}})}$ was explicitly identified in [Jia] as the closure of the minimal nilpotent orbit in $\mathfrak{so}_{8}$ (this was also studied earlier by Levasseur-Stafford in [LS], as well as Kazhdan in [Kaz] in the present context of restriction along $T\subseteq\mathrm{PGL}_{3}$ ). The action of $W=\Sigma_{3}$ on $\overline{T^{\ast}(\mathrm{SL}_{3}/{\check{{N}}})}$ can then be identified as the $\Sigma_{3}$ -action coming from triality on $\mathfrak{so}_{8}$ .

Let us observe now that the criteria (a) and (b) of Theorem 3.6.4 can be checked to hold (see below), if we set ${\check{{M}}}=\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}$ ; this suggests that 3.16 might indeed hold, if the left-hand side were sufficiently well-behaved. (See also [GR3, Theorem 2.3.1].)

First, we will show Theorem 3.6.4(b). The relevant Kostant section can be defined as follows. Fix a nondegenerate character $\psi:{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}\to\mathbf{G}_{a}$ , and define the map

$$ \kappa:{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Ind}^{{\check{{G}}}}_{{\check{{N}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}\hookrightarrow\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}, $$

where the first map is given by the inclusion ${\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\subseteq{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\oplus{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\ast}$ sending $x\mapsto(x,\psi)$ . Then, there is an isomorphism

$$ \displaystyle{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\times_{{\check{{M}}}/({\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{T}}})}{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast} \displaystyle\cong{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\times_{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})/({\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{T}}})}{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast} \displaystyle\cong{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}. $$

It follows from the main result of [ABG], or equivalently [YZ, Theorem 6.1] (see also [Dev2, Section 4.1] for a $2$ -periodified analogue), that there is an isomorphism

$$ {\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\cong\spec\mathrm{H}^{T}_{\ast}(\Omega G;\mathbf{Q}) $$

of graded group schemes over ${\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}$ . This implies Theorem 3.6.4(b).

It remains to check Theorem 3.6.4(a). For this, we need to check that there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathcal{O}_{({\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{T}}}\times{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast})/({\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast})}\cong\mathcal{O}_{\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}}. $$

The ${\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{T}}}$ -orbit of the image of $\kappa:{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\to T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})$ is the regular locus $T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})^{\mathrm{reg}}$ , so that there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathcal{O}_{({\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{T}}}\times{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast})/({\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast})}\cong\mathcal{O}_{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})^{\mathrm{reg}}}. $$

The inclusion $T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})$ has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ , since it can be identified with the inclusion $\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{N}}}}^{{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{N}}}}^{{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}$ ; the claim follows from Lemma 4.3.10(a) along with the observation that the inclusion ${\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}^{\ast}$ has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ . The inclusion $T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})\subseteq\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}$ also has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ (e.g., by Lemma 4.3.10(b)), so that there are isomorphisms

$$ \mathcal{O}_{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})^{\mathrm{reg}}}\cong\mathcal{O}_{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}\cong\mathcal{O}_{\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})}} $$

by the algebraic Hartogs lemma. This verifies Theorem 3.6.4(a), as desired.

#### Remark 3.6.14.

One can extend Example 3.6.13 to more general Levi subgroups as follows. Let $I\subseteq{\check{{\Delta}}}$ denote a subset of the simple roots of $G$ , let $P_{I}$ denote the associated parabolic subgroup, and let $L_{I}\subseteq P_{I}$ denote a fixed Levi factor. The subset $I$ defines a subset of simple roots of ${\check{{G}}}$ , which we will also denote by $I$ (for simplicity). Following [Mac], let $\psi_{I}:{\check{{N}}}\to\mathbf{G}_{a}$ denote the additive character given by the composite

$$ {\check{{N}}}\to{\check{{N}}}/[{\check{{N}}},{\check{{N}}}]\cong\prod_{\Delta}\mathbf{G}_{a}\xrightarrow{{\proj_{I}}}\prod_{I}\mathbf{G}_{a}\xrightarrow{{\sum}}\mathbf{G}_{a}, $$

so that $\psi_{I}$ defines an element of ${\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\ast}$ . This allows one to define the Whittaker reduction $T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/_{\psi_{I}}{\check{{N}}})$ , which admits a natural ${\check{{G}}}$ -action. Let $\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/_{\psi_{I}}{\check{{N}}})}$ denote its affine closure. We then expect the following:

Let $L_{I}$ denote the above Levi subgroup of $G$ . Then there is an isomorphism

$$ \overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/_{\psi_{I}}{\check{{N}}})}\cong\overline{({\check{{G}}}\times{\check{{\mathfrak{l}}}}_{I}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{L}}}_{I})/{\check{{J}}}_{X}}, $$

where ${\check{{J}}}_{X}=\spec\mathrm{H}^{L_{I}}_{\ast}(\Omega(G/L_{I});k)$ (so that ${\check{{J}}}_{X}$ can be identified with the kernel of the homomorphism ${\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{G}}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{l}}}}_{I}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{L}}}_{I}\to{\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{L}}}_{I}}$ as in 3.17).

which is equivariant for the left-action of $\mathrm{Shv}_{(G\times G)[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{G}}})$ via Theorem 3.2.7; we have again omitted the grading on the spectral side for simplicity.

If the hypotheses of Theorem 3.6.4 are satisfied for $L_{I}\subseteq G$ , the equivalence of categories in Conjecture 3.6.15 follows from the first isomorphism therein. In future work [DG2] with Tom Gannon, we will address the first part of Conjecture 3.6.15 using “Whittaker descent”.

When $L_{I}$ is spherical2323 23 Note that there is a classification of spherical Levi subgroups of simple linear algebraic groups using Krämer’s classification [Kra]; see [Bru, Theorem 4.1]. For instance, if $G$ is a classical group, the only possibilities are $\mathrm{GL}_{j}\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-j}\subseteq\mathrm{GL}_{j}$ , $\mathrm{SO}_{2}\times\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ , $\mathrm{GL}_{n}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ , $\mathbf{G}_{m}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}\subseteq\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$ , $\mathrm{GL}_{n}\subseteq\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$ , $\mathrm{SO}_{2}\times\mathrm{SO}_{2n-2}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ , and $\mathrm{GL}_{n}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ ., the relationship between the spectral side of Conjecture 3.6.15 and the predicted dual variety of Conjecture 3.4.12 seems to be very nontrivial. Let us remark on one interesting consequence of Conjecture 3.6.15. Write $\mathrm{N}_{G}(L_{I})$ to denote the normalizer of $L_{I}\subseteq G$ . There is a natural action of the relative Weyl group $W_{I}=\mathrm{N}_{G}(L_{I})/L_{I}$ on the left-hand side of Conjecture 3.6.15, which defines an action of $W_{I}$ on the right-hand side. $$ \mathrm{Shv}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}_{G[\![t]\!]}(G(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{N}_{G}(L_{I})(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}(\overline{T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/_{\psi_{I}}{\check{{N}}})}/W_{I})/{\check{{G}}}). $$

#### Proposition 3.6.16.

Let $H\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup. Then there is a Lagrangian correspondence (interpreted in a derived sense)

$$ \textstyle{{\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{G}}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{{\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{H}}}}} \textstyle{{\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{G}}}},} $$

where the left map restricts to the zero section of ${\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{H}}}}$ when pulled back to the identity section of ${\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{G}}}}$ .

#### Proof.

The desired claim follows from the analogous statement at the level of Lie algebras. It is a classical fact that the Lie algebra of ${\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{G}}}}$ can be identified with the cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}})\cong T^{\ast}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}})$ , and similarly for ${\check{{J}}}_{{\check{{H}}}}$ . We therefore need to see that there is a Lagrangian correspondence

$$ \textstyle{T^{\ast}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}})\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{T^{\ast}({\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}})} \textstyle{T^{\ast}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}).} $$

More generally, if $Y\to Z$ is a map between schemes, there is a Lagrangian correspondence

$$ \textstyle{T^{\ast}(Z)\times_{Z}Y\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{T^{\ast}Y} \textstyle{T^{\ast}Z.} $$

This is of course well-known if $Y\to Z$ is a smooth map of smooth schemes, but the same continues to hold in general (see, e.g., [Cal2, Theorem 2.8]). Taking $Y\to Z$ to be the map ${\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}$ , we win. ∎

Assume now that ${\check{{\mathcal{M}}}}^{\ddagger}\cong{\check{{\mathcal{M}}}}$ , and similarly ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}\cong{\check{{M}}}$ .
