#### Lemma 4.3.5.

There is a homotopy equivalence $(\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}/\mathrm{GL}_{n})(\mathbf{C})\simeq S^{2n+1}$ . Furthermore, if $B\subseteq G$ is the subgroup of upper-triangular matrices, the Levi quotient $L(X)$ of the parabolic subgroup stabilizing the open $B$ -orbit in $\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}/\mathrm{GL}_{n}$ is given by $\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}\times\mathbf{G}_{m}^{\times 2}$ .

#### Lemma 4.3.6.

There is an isomorphism of graded $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}$ -algebras

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{U}(n)}\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta,c_{1},\cdots,c_{n},\tfrac{1}{1+\beta c_{1}+\cdots+\beta^{n}c_{n}}]\cong\mathcal{O}_{T^{n}_{\beta}/\!\!/\Sigma_{n}}, $$

where $c_{j}$ lives in weight $-2j$ .

#### Proof.

Let $T^{n}$ denote the standard diagonal torus of $\mathrm{U}(n)$ , so that

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T^{n}}\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta,x_{1},\cdots,x_{n},\prod_{i=1}^{n}\tfrac{1}{1+\beta x_{i}}]. $$

Since the Weyl group of $T^{n}$ inside $\mathrm{U}(n)$ is the symmetric group $\Sigma_{n}$ , Proposition 2.3.15 says that $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{U}(n)}\cong(\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T^{n}})^{\Sigma_{n}}$ . The action of $\Sigma_{n}$ on $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{T^{n}}$ is simply given by permuting the $x_{j}$ . If we set $c_{j}$ to denote the $j$ th elementary symmetric polynomial in the variables $x_{1},\cdots,x_{n}$ , the lemma follows immediately. ∎

#### Proposition 4.3.7.

There is an isomorphism of graded $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{U}(n)}$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{ku}_{\ast}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega S^{2n+1})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta,c_{1},\cdots,c_{n},\tfrac{1}{1+\beta c_{1}+\cdots+\beta^{n}c_{n}},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-1}{c_{n}}], $$

where $c_{j}$ lives in weight $-2j$ and $a$ lives in weight $0$ .

#### Proof.

By Corollary 4.2.17, $\mathrm{ku}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n+1})\cong\mathrm{ku}^{T^{n}}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n+1})^{\Sigma_{n}}$ . As a $T^{n}$ -representation, $S^{2n+1}$ is the one-point compactification of $V=\mathbf{R}\oplus\bigoplus_{j=1}^{n}\mathrm{std}_{j}$ . Theorem 4.2.13 says that

$$ \mathrm{ku}^{T^{n}}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n+1})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta,x_{1},\cdots,x_{n},\prod_{i=1}^{n}\tfrac{1}{1+\beta x_{i}},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-1}{x_{1}\cdots x_{n}}], $$

so since the action of $\Sigma_{n}$ simply permutes the $x_{j}$ and leaves $y$ invariant, we see from Lemma 4.3.6 (and $c_{n}=x_{1}\cdots x_{n}$ ) that

$$ \mathrm{ku}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n+1})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta,c_{1},\cdots,c_{n},\tfrac{1}{1+\beta c_{1}+\cdots+\beta^{n}c_{n}},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-1}{c_{n}}], $$

as desired. ∎

#### Corollary 4.3.8.

There is an isomorphism of graded $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{U}(n)}$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{ku}_{\ast}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega{\mathbf{C}P}^{n})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta,c_{1},\cdots,c_{n},\tfrac{1}{1+\beta c_{1}+\cdots+\beta^{n}c_{n}},b]/bc_{n}, $$

where $c_{j}$ lives in weight $-2j$ and $b$ lives in weight $2n$ .

#### Proof.

Let $V$ denote the $\mathrm{U}(n)$ -representation $\mathbf{C}^{n}$ , so that the $\mathrm{U}(n)$ action on ${\mathbf{C}P}^{n}$ is obtained by viewing it as ${\mathbf{C}P}(V\oplus\mathbf{R})$ . We then have the generalized $\mathrm{U}(n)$ -equivariant Hopf fibration

$$ S^{1}\to S^{V\oplus\mathbf{R}}\to{\mathbf{C}P}(V\oplus\mathbf{R}), $$

which induces a $\mathrm{U}(n)$ -equivariant fibration of ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ -spaces

$$ \Omega S^{1}\cong\mathbf{Z}\to\Omega S^{V\oplus\mathbf{R}}\to\Omega{\mathbf{C}P}(V\oplus\mathbf{R}). $$

This implies that there is an equivalence of ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $\mathrm{ku}_{\mathrm{U}(n)}$ -algebras

$$ \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega{\mathbf{C}P}^{n})^{\vee}\simeq\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega S^{2n+1})^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathrm{ku}[\Omega S^{1}]}\mathrm{ku}. $$

$$ \mathrm{ku}_{\ast}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega{\mathbf{C}P}^{n})\cong\mathrm{ku}_{\ast}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega S^{2n+1})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta,a^{\pm 1}]}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta]\cong\mathrm{ku}_{\ast}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega S^{2n+1})/(a-1). $$

The desired result follows from the calculation of Proposition 4.3.7: the class $\tfrac{a-1}{c_{n}}\in\mathrm{ku}_{\ast}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega S^{2n+1})$ is sent to the class denoted $b\in\mathrm{ku}_{2n}^{\mathrm{U}(n)}(\Omega{\mathbf{C}P}^{n})$ under the generalized Hopf fibration. ∎

#### Lemma 4.3.10.

The following statements hold:

- (a) Let $G_{2}\subseteq G_{1}$ be a closed subgroup scheme. Let $Y\to Z$ be an open immersion of schemes with $G_{2}$ -action whose complement has codimension $\geq d$ . Then the induced map $\mathrm{Ind}_{G_{2}}^{G_{1}}Y\to\mathrm{Ind}_{G_{2}}^{G_{1}}Z$ is an open immersion of schemes with $G_{1}$ -action whose complement has codimension $\geq d$ .

- (b) Let $Y$ be an integral quasi-affine variety such that $\pi_{0}\Gamma(Y;\mathcal{O}_{Y})$ is Noetherian. Then the map $Y\to\overline{Y}$ to its affine closure is an open immersion whose complement has codimension $\geq 2$ .

#### Proof.

Part (a) is clear. For part (b), let $Z\subseteq\overline{Y}$ denote a closed subscheme of $Y$ associated to a minimal prime in the complement of $Y\subseteq\overline{Y}$ , so that $Y\subseteq\overline{Y}-Z$ . Then there are maps

$$ \mathrm{H}^{0}(\mathcal{O}_{\overline{Y}})\xrightarrow{{f}}\mathrm{H}^{0}(\mathcal{O}_{\overline{Y}-Z})\xrightarrow{{g}}\mathrm{H}^{0}(\mathcal{O}_{Y}). $$

The map $g$ is an isomorphism, and the composite is also an isomorphism (by assumption). Therefore, $f$ is also an isomorphism. We claim that this forces $\mathfrak{q}$ is necessarily of height $\geq 2$ . Indeed, let $A=\mathrm{H}^{0}(\mathcal{O}_{\overline{Y}})$ , so that $A$ is Noetherian. The desired claim then follows from the more general observation: if $A$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak{p}\subseteq A$ is a height one prime ideal corresponding to a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq\spec(A)$ with complement $U\subseteq\spec(A)$ , the inclusion $A\subseteq\Gamma(\mathcal{O}_{U})$ is strict. To see this, standard arguments reduce us to the case when $A$ is local. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $\mathfrak{p}$ is the radical of any nonzero $a\in\mathfrak{p}$ . Therefore, the inclusion $A\subseteq\Gamma(\mathcal{O}_{U})$ corresponds to the inclusion $A\subseteq A[1/a]$ , which is evidently strict. ∎

#### Corollary 4.3.19.

Let $G=\mathrm{PGL}_{n+1}$ and $H=\mathrm{GL}_{n}$ , so ${\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{SL}_{n+1}$ and ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . There is an equivalence of $\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}(\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta])$ -linear $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{ku})^{\mathrm{faux}}\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}_{\beta}/\mathrm{SL}_{n+1}[-2\rho]). $$

When $\beta=0$ , this specializes to an equivalence of $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(T^{\ast}[2n](\mathbf{A}^{2}[2n,0])/\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-2n\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]\times\mathfrak{gl}_{n-1}[2]/\!\!/\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}). $$

#### Proof.

Recall that $\mathrm{PGL}_{n+1}=\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}/\mathrm{GL}_{1}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ , so that there are equivalences (where the second line comes from Corollary 4.3.17)

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{n+1}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{PGL}_{n+1}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{GL}_{n}(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{ku})^{\mathrm{faux}}\\
\simeq\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{GL}_{n}(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{ku})^{\mathrm{faux}}\otimes_{\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{GL}_{1}[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{GL}_{1}(\!(t)\!);\mathrm{ku})^{\mathrm{faux}}}\mathrm{LMod}_{\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta]}\\
\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}_{\beta}/\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}[-2\rho])\otimes_{\mathrm{Perf}(B\mathbf{G}_{m})}\mathrm{LMod}_{\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta]}\\
\simeq\mathrm{Perf}\left(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}_{\beta}/\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}[-2\rho]\times_{B\mathbf{G}_{m}}\spec\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[\beta]\right) $$

However, the displayed fiber product is precisely $\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}_{\beta}/\mathrm{SL}_{n+1}[-2\rho]$ . The claim about identifying its reduction modulo $\beta$ with $T^{\ast}[2n](\mathbf{A}^{2}[2n,0])/\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-2\rho_{\mathrm{SL}_{2}}]\times\mathfrak{gl}_{n-1}[2]/\!\!/\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}$ follows from the construction of ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}_{\beta}$ . ∎

#### Remark 4.3.20.

In the case of the spherical variety $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}/\mathbf{G}_{m}$ , Corollary 4.3.19 states that there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{PGL}_{2}(\!(t)\!)/\mathbf{G}_{m}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(T^{\ast}[2n](\mathbf{A}^{2}[2n,0])/\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-2n\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]). $$

The $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ -variety $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}/\mathbf{G}_{m}$ has a natural action of the Weyl group $\mathbf{Z}/2=\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}}(\mathbf{G}_{m})/\mathbf{G}_{m}$ (under the homotopy equivalence $(\mathrm{PGL}_{2}/\mathbf{G}_{m})(\mathbf{C})\simeq S^{2}$ , this is the antipodal action). This equips the left-hand side of the above equivalence with a natural $\mathbf{Z}/2$ -action. One can show that under this equivalence, the resulting $\mathbf{Z}/2$ -action on the right-hand side identifies with the natural $\mathbf{Z}/2$ -action on $T^{\ast}(\mathbf{A}^{2})$ via the symplectic form. That is, the action sends

$$ (v_{1},v_{2}),(w_{1},w_{2})\mapsto(-w_{2},w_{1}),(v_{2},-v_{1}). $$

See Conjecture 3.6.15 and the surrounding discussion for an expected generalization to arbitrary semisimple algebraic groups. The normalizer $\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}}(\mathbf{G}_{m})$ can be identified with $\mathrm{PO}_{2}$ , which implies that there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{PGL}_{2}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{PO}_{2}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(T^{\ast}[2](\mathbf{A}^{2}[2,0])/(\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-2\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]\times\mathbf{Z}/2)). $$

Note that the spherical root of $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}/\mathrm{PO}_{2}$ is (by definition) of type N, and so the spherical $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ -variety $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}/\mathrm{PO}_{2}$ is excluded by [SV, BZSV]. Nevertheless, the preceding equivalence shows that the Hamiltonian $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -“space” which should be dual (in the sense of [BZSV]) to $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}/\mathrm{PO}_{2}$ is the stack $T^{\ast}(\mathbf{A}^{2})/(\mathbf{Z}/2)$ .

### 4.4. Type $B_{n}$ : $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$

Our goal in this section is to prove Theorem 3.4.16 in type $B_{n}$ , i.e., for the spherical $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ -variety $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ . Note that if $(V,q)$ is a quadratic space and $v\in V$ with $q(v)=1$ , then $\mathrm{SO}_{V}/\mathrm{SO}_{v^{\perp}}$ can be identified with the hyperboloid $\{w\in V|q(w)=1\}$ . Write $G=\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ and $H=\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ , so that ${\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$ . Recall from Table 3 that ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . In this section, we will only consider coefficients in $\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}$ (instead of $\mathrm{ku}$ ).

#### Theorem 4.4.1 (Theorem 3.4.16 in type $B_{n}$ ).

There is an equivalence of $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(T^{\ast}[2n](\mathbf{A}^{2}[4n-2,0])/\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-(4n-2)\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]\times\mathfrak{sp}_{2n-2}[2]/\!\!/\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}). $$

The proof of Theorem 4.4.1 will take up the remainder of this section.

#### Lemma 4.4.2.

There is a homotopy equivalence $(\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n})(\mathbf{C})\simeq S^{2n}$ . Moreover, if $B\subseteq G$ is the Borel subgroup of upper-triangular matrices, the Levi quotient $L(X)$ of the parabolic subgroup stabilizing the open $B$ -orbit in $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ is given by $\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}\times\mathbf{G}_{m}$ .

#### Lemma 4.4.3.

Let $W=(\mathbf{Z}/2)^{n-1}\rtimes\Sigma_{n}$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ . Then there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},c_{n}], $$

where the injective map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{T^{n}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ sends $p_{j}$ to the $j$ th elementary symmetric polynomial in the variables $x_{1}^{2},\cdots,x_{n-1}^{2}$ (so $p_{j}$ lives in weight $-4j$ ), and $c_{n}\mapsto x_{1}\cdots x_{n}$ .

#### Proposition 4.4.4.

There is a graded isomorphism of $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},c_{n},b]/bc_{n}, $$

where $b$ lives in weight $4n-2$ . (In particular, $\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ is not flat over $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ .)

#### Proof.

The restriction of the $\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ -action on $S^{2n}$ to the maximal torus $T^{n}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ exhibits $S^{2n}$ as the one-point compactification of the standard $n$ -dimensional complex representation $\mathrm{std}$ . Corollary 4.2.17 implies that there is a graded isomorphism of $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\left(\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n},b]/bx_{1}\cdots x_{n}\right)^{W}, $$

where $b$ lives in weight $4n-2$ . The $W$ -invariants on the right-hand side can be computed using Lemma 4.4.3 (note that the action of $W$ on $b$ is trivial), and gives the desired calculation. ∎

#### Definition 4.4.5.

Let ${\check{{V}}}$ denote the graded affine space $\mathbf{A}^{1}(2-2n)\times\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W$ . There is an action of $\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)$ on ${\check{{V}}}$ , where $\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\ 0&1\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)$ sends $(z,\vec{p},c_{n})\mapsto(z-bc_{n},\vec{p},c_{n})$ . Note that $b$ lives in weight $4n-2$ .

Equip ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ with the grading coming from $(4n-2)\rho_{\mathrm{SL}_{2}}$ , so that the entries of a matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{pmatrix}$ are equipped with the following weights: $a$ and $d$ have weight $0$ , $b$ has weight $4n-2$ , and $c$ has weight $2-4n$ . Let $V$ denote the affine space $\mathbf{A}^{2}(4n-2,0)$ , so that there is an action of ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ on ${\check{{V}}}$ via

$$ \begin{pmatrix}a&b\\
c&d\end{pmatrix}\cdot(x,y)=(ax+cy,bx+dy); $$

here, $x$ lives in degree $2-4n$ and $y$ lives in degree $0$ . There is an isomorphism

$$ \mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)\backslash{\check{{G}}}_{X}\cong{\check{{V}}}-\{0\},\ \begin{pmatrix}a&b\\
c&d\end{pmatrix}\mapsto(c,d), $$

and the above action of ${\check{{G}}}_{X}$ on ${\check{{V}}}$ restricts on ${\check{{V}}}-\{0\}$ to the right-action of ${\check{{G}}}_{X}$ on $\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)\backslash{\check{{G}}}_{X}$ .

Let $\kappa:\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\to{\check{{V}}}$ denote the map sending $(\vec{p},c_{n})\mapsto(0,\vec{p},c_{n})$ . Let $W^{\prime}$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}$ , so Lemma 4.3.18 implies that there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{Ind}_{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}^{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}{\check{{V}}}\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times T^{\ast}(2n)(V-\{0\}). $$

In particular, there is an open immersion

$$ \mathrm{Ind}_{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}^{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}{\check{{V}}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times T^{\ast}(2n)(V) $$

which exhibits the target as the affine closure of $\mathrm{Ind}_{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}^{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}{\check{{V}}}$ . Inducing along the map ${\check{{G}}}_{X}\to{\check{{G}}}$ produces an open immersion

$$ \mathrm{Ind}_{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}^{{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{V}}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}}T^{\ast}(2n)(V), $$

and we will write ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}=\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}}T^{\ast}(2n)(V)$ .

The map $\kappa$ defines a locally closed immersion

$$ \mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\xrightarrow{{\kappa}}{\check{{V}}}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Ind}_{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}^{{\check{{G}}}}{\check{{V}}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}}T^{\ast}(2n)(V)={\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}, $$

which we will denote by $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}}$ .

#### Remark 4.4.6.

In Definition 4.4.5, it does not make sense to ask that $\kappa:\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\to{\check{{V}}}$ instead send $(\vec{p},c_{n})\mapsto(1,\vec{p},c_{n})$ . Indeed, the point $1\in\mathbf{A}^{1}(2-2n)$ is not well-defined, since it would have to be cut out by the ideal $(z-1)$ , which is not homogeneous (i.e., is not a graded ideal).

#### Proposition 4.4.7.

Let $C=\mathbf{A}^{1}=\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[c]$ , and let $\mathbf{A}^{2}=\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[z,c]$ . Let $\underline{\mathbf{G}_{a}}$ denote the constant group scheme over $C$ acting on $\mathbf{A}^{2}$ by $b\cdot(z,c)=(z+bc,c)$ . Let $f:C\to Y$ denote the map $c\mapsto(0,c)$ , and let $J$ denote the stabilizer group scheme of the image of $f$ (over $C$ ). Then $J$ is not flat over $C$ , and the quotient $\underline{\mathbf{G}_{a}}/J$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf{A}^{2}-\{0\}$ . Moreover, if $\underline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}}$ is the constant group scheme over $C$ with $J\subseteq\underline{\mathbf{G}_{a}}$ embedded via the upper-triangular matrices, the affine closure of $\underline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}}/J$ can be identified with $T^{\ast}\mathbf{A}^{2}$ .

#### Proof.

It is immediate that $J\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[b,c]/bc$ , so is not flat over $C$ . (This implies that the $\underline{\mathbf{G}_{a}}$ -orbit of the image of $f$ is only a constructible subset of $\mathbf{A}^{2}$ : indeed, this $\underline{\mathbf{G}_{a}}$ -orbit is the standard example $(\mathbf{A}^{2}-\{z=0\})\cup\{(0,0)\}$ of a constructible subset.) For the claim about $\underline{\mathbf{G}_{a}}/J$ , let $\mathrm{Mir}_{2}\subseteq\mathrm{GL}_{2}$ denote (as usual) the mirabolic subgroup of matrices of the form $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ 0&1\end{pmatrix}$ , let $\underline{\mathrm{Mir}_{2}}$ denote the constant group scheme over $C$ , and let $\widetilde{J}\subseteq\mathrm{Mir}_{2}$ denote the subgroup of matrices cut out by the equation $a-1=bc$ . Then $\underline{\mathbf{G}_{a}}$ (resp. $J$ ) is the kernel of the determinant $\underline{\mathrm{Mir}_{2}}\xrightarrow{{\mathrm{det}}}\underline{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ (resp. $\widetilde{J}\to\underline{\mathrm{Mir}_{2}}\xrightarrow{{\mathrm{det}}}\underline{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ ). This implies that $\underline{\mathbf{G}_{a}}/J\cong\underline{\mathrm{Mir}_{2}}/\widetilde{J}$ , and the latter is isomorphic to $\mathbf{A}^{2}-\{0\}$ via the map $\underline{\mathrm{Mir}_{2}}\to\mathbf{A}^{2}-\{0\}$ sending $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ 0&1\end{pmatrix},c\mapsto(a+bc,c)$ , as desired. (In the $\beta$ -deformed case, this is Proposition 4.3.12.) Next, there is an isomorphism ${\mathrm{SL}_{2}}/{\mathbf{G}_{a}}\cong\mathbf{A}^{2}-\{0\}$ , which implies that $\underline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}}/J\cong\underline{\mathrm{GL}_{2}}/\widetilde{J}$ is isomorphic to the complement of the zero section in $T^{\ast}(\mathbf{A}^{2}-\{0\})$ . (It can alternatively be described as $\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times^{\mathbf{G}_{a}}(\mathbf{A}^{2}-\{0\})$ .) Its affine closure is $T^{\ast}(\mathbf{A}^{2})$ , as claimed. ∎

#### Proposition 4.4.8.

There is an isomorphism of graded group schemes over $\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W$ :

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SO}_{2n}}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W. $$

Moreover, if ${\check{{J}}}_{X}$ denotes the above group scheme over $\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W$ , the algebra of regular functions on $(\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\times{\check{{G}}})/{\check{{J}}}_{X}$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}}$ .

#### Proof.

There is an isomorphism

$$ \mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{V}}}/\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W, $$

as well as a closed immersion

$$ \mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{V}}}/\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\times\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n), $$

which exhibits $\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{V}}}/\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W$ as the subscheme of pairs $(\vec{p},c_{n},b)$ such that $b$ stabilizes $\kappa(\vec{p},c_{n})$ . But by definition of $\kappa$ , this happens if and only if $bc_{n}=0$ . In other words, there is an isomorphism of graded schemes over $\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W$ :

$$ \mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{V}}}/\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}\mathfrak{t}^{n}(2)/\!\!/W\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},c_{n},b]/bc_{n}. $$

The first part of the proposition therefore follows from Proposition 4.4.4. The second part of the proposition follows from Proposition 4.4.7 (rather, its obvious variant for graded affine spaces). ∎

#### Proof of Theorem 4.4.1.

This follows from Theorem 3.6.4 and Proposition 4.4.8, along with the isomorphism between ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)$ and $T^{\ast}(2n)(V)/{\check{{G}}}_{X}(-(4n-2)\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})\times\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}$ . ∎

#### Remark 4.4.9.

Theorem 4.4.1 can be used to prove a variant for the rank one spherical $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ -variety $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}/\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}}(\mathrm{SO}_{2n})$ , where $\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}}(\mathrm{SO}_{2n})$ is the normalizer of $\mathrm{SO}_{2n}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ . The dual group ${\check{{G}}}_{X}$ in this case is again $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . The quotient $\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}}(\mathrm{SO}_{2n})/\mathrm{SO}_{2n}$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf{Z}/2$ , and it acts on $(\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n})(\mathbf{C})\simeq S^{2n}$ via the antipodal action. As in Remark 4.3.20, this equips the left-hand side of the equivalence of Theorem 4.4.1 with a natural $\mathbf{Z}/2$ -action. One can show that under this equivalence, the resulting $\mathbf{Z}/2$ -action on the right-hand side of Theorem 4.4.1 identifies with the natural $\mathbf{Z}/2$ -action on $T^{\ast}(\mathbf{A}^{2})$ via the symplectic form. Using this, one finds that there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}}(\mathrm{SO}_{2n})(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\\
\mathrm{Perf}(T^{\ast}[2n](\mathbf{A}^{2}[4n-2,0])/(\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-(4n-2)\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]\times\mathbf{Z}/2)\times\mathfrak{sp}_{2n-2}[2]/\!\!/\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}). $$

The spherical root of $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}/\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}}(\mathrm{SO}_{2n})$ is of type N, and so it is excluded by [SV, BZSV]; nevertheless, the preceding equivalence shows that it does admit a dual, given by the stack $\mathrm{Ind}_{\mathrm{SL}_{2}}^{\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}}(T^{\ast}(\mathbf{A}^{2})/(\mathbf{Z}/2)\times\mathbf{A}^{n-1})$ .

### 4.5. Type $C_{n}$ : $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}/(\mathrm{Sp}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2})$

Our goal in this section is to prove Theorem 3.4.16 in type $C_{n}$ , i.e., for the spherical $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$ -variety $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}/(\mathrm{Sp}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2})$ . Let $G=\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$ and $H=\mathrm{Sp}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}$ , so that ${\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ . Recall from Table 3 that ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ .

#### Theorem 4.5.1 (Theorem 3.4.16 in type $C_{n}$ ).

There is an equivalence of $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(T^{\ast}[4n-4](\mathbf{A}^{2}[4n-2,0])/\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-(4n-2)\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]\times{\check{{\mathfrak{h}}}}^{\ast}[2]/\!\!/{\check{{H}}}), $$

where $H=\mathrm{Sp}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2(n-2)}$ .

The proof of Theorem 4.5.1 will take up the remainder of this section.

#### Lemma 4.5.2.

There is a homotopy equivalence $(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}/(\mathrm{Sp}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}))(\mathbf{C})\simeq\mathbf{H}P^{n-1}$ . Moreover, if $B\subseteq G$ is the Borel subgroup of upper-triangular matrices, the Levi quotient $L(X)$ of the parabolic subgroup stabilizing the open $B$ -orbit in $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}/(\mathrm{Sp}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2})$ is given by $\mathrm{GL}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-4}$ .

#### Lemma 4.5.3.

Let $W$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$ . Then there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathbf{Q}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n}], $$

where the map $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\to\mathrm{H}_{T^{n}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ sends $p_{j}$ to the $j$ th elementary symmetric polynomial in the variables $x_{1}\overline{x}_{1},\cdots,x_{n}\overline{x}_{n}$ . Here, $\overline{x}=-x$ .

Although one can give an argument for the following result using Theorem 4.2.13, it is simpler to give an argument “from scratch”.

#### Proposition 4.5.4.

There is an isomorphism of graded $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1};\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathbf{Q}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},b]/bp_{n-1}, $$

where $b$ lives in weight $4n-2$ .

#### Proof.

Let $T^{n-1}\subseteq\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}$ denote the maximal torus. Then the homotopy fixed points spectral sequence for $\pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}[\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1}]^{hT^{n-1}}$ is given by

$$ E_{2}^{\ast,\ast}\cong\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1};\mathbf{Q})\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}\pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}^{hT^{n-1}}\Rightarrow\pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}[\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1}]^{hT^{n-1}}. $$

To compute the $E_{2}$ -page, observe that the Hopf fibration $S^{3}\to S^{4n-1}\to\mathbf{H}P^{n-1}$ implies that there is an equivalence $\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1}\simeq S^{3}\times\Omega S^{4n-1}$ . This gives an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1};\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathbf{Q}[a,b]/a^{2}, $$

where $a$ lives in weight $3$ and $b$ lives in weight $4n-2$ . Therefore,

$$ E_{2}^{\ast,\ast}\cong\mathbf{Q}[a,b][\![x_{1},\cdots,x_{n-1}]\!]/a^{2}, $$

where each $x_{j}$ lives in weight $-2$ . Recall that the action of $T^{n-1}$ on $\mathbf{H}P^{n-1}$ is induced by the inclusion $T^{n-1}\subseteq\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}\subseteq\mathrm{U}(4n-4)$ given by the representation $\bigoplus_{j=1}^{n-1}\mathrm{std}\oplus\mathrm{std}^{-1}$ . This forces a single differential in the above spectral sequence, given by

$$ d_{2}(a)=bx_{1}\overline{x}_{1}\cdots x_{n-1}\overline{x}_{n-1}. $$

After running this differential, the spectral sequence is concentrated in even degrees, and we find that there is an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}[\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1}]^{hT^{n-1}}\cong\mathbf{Q}[b][\![x_{1},\cdots,x_{n-1}]\!]/bx_{1}\overline{x}_{1}\cdots x_{n-1}\overline{x}_{n-1}. $$

To calculate $\mathrm{H}^{T^{n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1};\mathbf{Q})$ itself (and not just its completion $\pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}[\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1}]^{hT^{n-1}}$ ), the strategy of Theorem 4.2.13 reduces us to showing that the restriction $\mathrm{H}^{T^{n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1};\mathbf{Q})|_{{\mathfrak{t}}^{\circ}}=\mathrm{H}_{T^{n-1}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ . By Lemma 2.4.6, there is an isomorphism $\mathrm{H}^{T^{n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1};\mathbf{Q})|_{{\mathfrak{t}}^{\circ}}\cong\mathrm{H}^{T^{n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega(\mathbf{H}P^{n-1};\mathbf{Q})^{T^{n-1}})|_{{\mathfrak{t}}^{\circ}}$ . It therefore suffices to show that $\Omega(\mathbf{H}P^{n-1})^{T^{n-1}}$ is contractible, but this is a consequence of the simple observation that $(\mathbf{H}P^{n-1})^{T^{n-1}}\cong S^{0}$ . This discussion gives an isomorphism of graded $\mathrm{H}_{T^{n-1}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{T^{n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{H}P^{n-1};\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathbf{Q}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n-1},b]/bx_{1}\overline{x}_{1}\cdots x_{n-1}\overline{x}_{n-1}. $$

This isomorphism is $W$ -equivariant (where $W$ is the Weyl group of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}$ ), so Proposition 2.3.15 implies that there is an isomorphism of graded $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -algebras

Noting that the action of $W$ leaves $b$ invariant, Lemma 4.5.3 computes the right-hand side; the resulting answer is precisely the right-hand side of the proposition. ∎

#### Notation 4.5.5.

Let $W$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}$ , so that it is the product of $\mathbf{Z}/2$ with the Weyl group of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}$ . #### Proposition 4.5.8.

There is an isomorphism of graded group schemes over $\mathfrak{t}^{n}/\!\!/W$ :

There is an isomorphism

Let $G=\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$ and $H=\mathrm{Sp}_{2}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2n-2}$ , so ${\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ and ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . There is an equivalence of $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}). $$

Recall that there is a ${\check{{G}}}_{X}$ -equivariant fibration

$$ \overline{\mathrm{Ind}_{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}^{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}{\check{{V}}}}\to\overline{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)\backslash{\check{{G}}}_{X}}\cong V $$

whose fibers are isomorphic to ${\check{{V}}}$ . By Lemma 4.3.18, this implies that $\overline{\mathrm{Ind}_{\mathbf{G}_{a}(2-4n)}^{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}{\check{{V}}}}\cong T^{\ast}(4n-4)(V)$ , and so

### 4.6. Type $D_{n}$ : $\mathrm{PSO}_{2n}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}$

Our goal in this section is to prove Theorem 3.4.16 in type $D_{n}$ , i.e., for the spherical $\mathrm{SO}_{2n}/\mu_{2}$ -variety $\mathrm{SO}_{2n}/\mu_{2}\cdot\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}$ . Write $G=\mathrm{SO}_{2n}/\mu_{2}$ and $H=\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}$ , so ${\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{Spin}_{2n}$ and ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{Spin}_{3}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . As a shorthand, we will write $N=2n-2$ .

#### Theorem 4.6.1 (Theorem 3.4.16 in type $D_{n}$ ).

There is an equivalence of $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathrm{Perf}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2}[N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]/\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]\times\mathfrak{spin}_{N-1}[2]/\!\!/\mathrm{Spin}_{N-1}). $$

#### Example 4.6.2.

If $n=2$ , Theorem 4.6.1 says that there is an equivalence of $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{(\mathrm{SO}_{4}/\mu_{2})[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}((\mathrm{SO}_{4}/\mu_{2})(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{SO}_{3}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathrm{Perf}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2}[2-2\rho]/\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-2\rho]). $$

By Example 3.4.11, the left-hand side can therefore be identified with $\mathrm{Shv}_{(\mathrm{SO}_{3}\times\mathrm{SO}_{3})[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{SO}_{3}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})$ , and the above equivalence is simply the derived Satake equivalence of Theorem 3.2.7 for $\mathrm{SO}_{3}$ .

The proof of Theorem 4.6.1 will occupy the remainder of this section.

#### Lemma 4.6.3.

There is a homotopy equivalence $(\mathrm{SO}_{2n}/\mu_{2}\cdot\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1})(\mathbf{C})\simeq\mathbf{R}P^{2n-1}$ . Furthermore, if $B\subseteq G$ is the Borel subgroup of upper-triangular matrices, the Levi quotient $L(X)$ of the parabolic subgroup stabilizing the open $B$ -orbit in $\mathrm{SO}_{2n}/\mu_{2}\cdot\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}$ is given by $\mathrm{SO}_{2n-2}/\mu_{2}\times\mathbf{G}_{m}$ .

#### Lemma 4.6.4.

Let $W=(\mathbf{Z}/2)^{n-1}\rtimes\Sigma_{n-1}$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}$ . Then there is an isomorphism of graded $\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1}]\cong\mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}/\!\!/W}, $$

where $p_{j}$ lives in weight $-4j$ . The map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{T^{n-1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ sends $p_{j}$ to the $j$ th elementary symmetric polynomial in the variables $x_{1}^{2},\cdots,x_{n-1}^{2}$ .

#### Proposition 4.6.5.

There is an isomorphism of graded $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{R}P^{2n-1};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n-1},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}x_{i}}]^{W}. $$

Here, the action of the $j$ th $\mathbf{Z}/2\subseteq(\mathbf{Z}/2)^{n-1}\subseteq W$ sends $x_{j}\mapsto-{x}_{j}$ and $a\mapsto a^{-1}$ , and the symmetric group acts by permuting the variables $x_{1}^{2},\cdots,x_{n-1}^{2}$ (and leaves $a$ invariant).

#### Proof.

The restriction of the $\mathrm{Spin}_{2n-1}$ -action on $\mathrm{Spin}_{2n}/\mathrm{Spin}_{2n-1}$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $S^{2n-1}$ ) to $T^{n-1}\subseteq\mathrm{Spin}_{2n-1}$ exhibits $S^{2n-1}$ as the one-point compactification of $\mathrm{std}\oplus\mathbf{R}$ , where $\mathrm{std}$ is the standard $(n-1)$ -dimensional complex representation of $T^{n-1}$ . Corollary 4.2.17 implies that there is a graded isomorphism of $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{Spin}_{2n-1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{Spin}_{2n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n-1};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n-1},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-1}{x_{1}\cdots x_{n-1}}]^{W}. $$

The calculation of $\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{R}P^{2n-1};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ is a consequence of the above description of $\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{Spin}_{2n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega S^{2n-1};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ , the fact that $\mathrm{Spin}_{2n-1}/\mu_{2}\cong\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}$ , and the fact that $S^{2n-1}/(\mathbf{Z}/2)\cong\mathbf{R}P^{2n-1}$ . ∎

#### Construction 4.6.6.

Let $W^{\prime}$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{Spin}_{N-1}$ . Equip $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ with the grading coming from $-N\rho$ , and consider the ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -scheme $\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ (where $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ acts only on the factor $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ , via the adjoint action). Define

$$ {\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}=\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}}\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}). $$

Let $\kappa:\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W\to\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ denote the closed immersion sending

$$ (p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1})\mapsto(p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-2}),\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\
p_{n-1}&0\end{pmatrix}. $$

There is a closed immersion

$$ \displaystyle\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}) \displaystyle\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}) \displaystyle\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}}\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})\cong{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}, $$

and hence $\kappa$ defines a closed immersion

$$ \mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W\xrightarrow{{\kappa}}\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})\to{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}. $$

We will denote the above map by $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}}$ .

#### Proposition 4.6.7.

The ${\check{{G}}}$ -orbit of the image of $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}}$ has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ . Moreover, there is an isomorphism of graded group schemes over $\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W$ :

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{R}P^{2n-1};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W. $$

In particular, the conditions of Theorem 3.6.4 hold for the spherical $\mathrm{SO}_{2n}/\mu_{2}$ -variety $\mathrm{SO}_{2n}/\mu_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{2n-1}$ .

#### Proof.

Let us denote by $Y$ the $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -orbit of the image of $\kappa:\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W\to\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ . Then $Y\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\mathrm{reg}}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ , and it is well-known that the complement of $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\mathfrak{sl}_{2}$ has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ . Applying Lemma 4.3.10 to the $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -equivariant inclusion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ and the map $\mathrm{SL}_{2}\to{\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{Spin}_{2n}$ , we conclude that the ${\check{{G}}}$ -orbit of the image of $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}}$ has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ .

To prove the second part of the proposition, Proposition 4.6.5 reduces us to showing that there is a graded isomorphism

$$ \spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n-1},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}x_{i}}]^{W}\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W. $$

The $j$ th copy of $\mathbf{Z}/2\subseteq(\mathbf{Z}/2)^{n-1}\subseteq W$ sends $x_{j}\mapsto-x_{j}$ and $a\mapsto a^{-1}$ , so there is an isomorphism

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n-1},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}x_{i}}]^{W} \displaystyle\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{n-1},a+a^{-1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{x_{1}\cdots x_{n-1}}] \displaystyle\cong\mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}}\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}}\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{n-1},a+a^{-1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{x_{1}\cdots x_{n-1}}], $$

where we recall that $p_{j}$ is the $j$ th elementary symmetric polynomial in the variables $x_{1}^{2},\cdots,x_{n-1}^{2}$ . In particular, $p_{n-1}=(x_{1}\cdots x_{n-1})^{2}$ .

On the other hand, there is a graded isomorphism

$$ \displaystyle\hskip-28.45274pt\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W \displaystyle\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{(\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}))/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-N\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{n-1}(2)/\!\!/W \displaystyle\cong\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times(\mathbf{A}^{1}(N)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)\times_{\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-N\rho)}\mathbf{A}^{1}(N)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)). $$

By construction, the map $\mathbf{A}^{1}(N)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)\to\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-N\rho)$ is precisely a shifted version of the Kostant slice, so the discussion in [Dev2, Remark B.4] implies that if we write $p_{n-1}$ to denote the coordinate on $\mathbf{A}^{1}(N)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)$ , there is an isomorphism

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{A}^{1}(N)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)\times_{\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-N\rho)}\mathbf{A}^{1}(N)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2) \displaystyle\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[c_{n-1},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{c_{n-1}}]^{\mathbf{Z}/2} \displaystyle\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[p_{n-1},a+a^{-1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{c_{n-1}}], $$

where $c_{n-1}^{2}=p_{n-1}$ . This, along with 4.12, implies 4.11; it is not difficult to observe that 4.11 is in fact an isomorphism of group schemes. ∎

#### Remark 4.6.8.

Using Proposition 4.6.5, one finds that there are isomorphisms

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{GL}_{n}}_{\ast}(\Omega(\mathrm{SO}_{2n+2}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1});\mathbf{Q})\cong\spec\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}}_{\ast}(\Omega(\mathrm{SO}_{2n+2}/\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1});\mathbf{Q})\otimes_{\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{GL}_{n}}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\\

#### Proof of Theorem 4.6.1.

This follows from Proposition 4.6.7 and Theorem 3.6.4, along with the identification between ${\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)$ and $\mathfrak{t}^{n-2}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(N-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})/{\check{{G}}}_{X}(-N\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ . ∎

### 4.7. Type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$ : $\mathrm{F}_{4}/\mathrm{Spin}_{9}$

Our goal in this section is to prove Theorem 3.4.16 in type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$ , i.e., for the spherical $\mathrm{F}_{4}$ -variety $\mathrm{F}_{4}/\mathrm{Spin}_{9}$ . #### Theorem 4.7.1 (Theorem 3.4.16 in type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$ ).

There is an equivalence of $\mathbf{Q}$ -linear $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(T^{\ast}[16](\mathbf{A}^{2}[22,0])/\mathrm{SL}_{2}[-22\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}]\times\mathfrak{sp}_{6}^{\ast}[2]/\!\!/\mathrm{Sp}_{6}). $$

The proof of Theorem 4.7.1 will take up the remainder of this section.

#### Lemma 4.7.2.

There is a homotopy equivalence $(\mathrm{F}_{4}/\mathrm{Spin}_{9})(\mathbf{C})\simeq\mathbf{O}P^{2}$ . Moreover, if $B\subseteq G$ is the Borel subgroup of upper-triangular matrices, the Levi quotient $L(X)$ of the parabolic subgroup stabilizing the open $B$ -orbit in $\mathrm{F}_{4}/\mathrm{Spin}_{9}$ is given by $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}\times\mathbf{G}_{m}$ .

#### Proposition 4.7.3.

Let $W=(\mathbf{Z}/2)^{4}\rtimes\Sigma_{4}$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{Spin}_{9}$ . There is an isomorphism of graded $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Spin}_{9}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{Spin}_{9}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathbf{Q}[p_{1},\cdots,p_{4},b]/bp_{4}, $$

where $b$ lives in weight $22$ .

#### Proof.

The argument is essentially the same as that of the preceding subsections. Let $T^{4}\subseteq\mathrm{Spin}_{9}$ denote the maximal torus; we will begin by describing $\mathrm{H}^{T^{4}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})$ . The homotopy fixed points spectral sequence for $\pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}[\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2}]^{hT^{4}}$ is given by

$$ E_{2}^{\ast,\ast}\cong\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{H}_{T^{4}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})\Rightarrow\pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}[\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2}]^{hT^{4}}. $$

To compute the $E_{2}$ -page, we need to compute $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})$ . Using the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence, we will first calculate $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})$ . Although there is no Hopf fibration $S^{7}\to S^{23}\to\mathbf{O}P^{2}$ (otherwise, the cofiber of the map $S^{23}\to\mathbf{O}P^{2}$ would provide a contradiction to the Hopf invariant one problem), we can instead compute $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})$ using the Serre spectral sequence for the fibration

$$ \Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2}\to\ast\to\mathbf{O}P^{2} $$

and the fact that $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})$ is isomorphic to a free graded $\mathbf{Q}$ -module on classes $\{1,x_{1},x_{2}\}$ in weights $0$ , $8$ , and $16$ . This is a standard argument: one finds that $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathbf{Q}[a,b]/a^{2}$ where $a$ lives in weight $7$ and $b$ lives in weight $22$ ; the differentials in the Serre spectral sequence are given by

$$ d^{8}(b^{j}x_{1})=ab^{j},\ d^{8}(b^{j}x_{2})=ab^{j}x_{1},\ d^{23}(ab^{j}x_{2})=b^{j+1}. $$

The Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence for $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})$ degenerates at the $E_{1}$ -page (with no multiplicative extensions), and we obtain an isomorphism $\mathrm{H}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathbf{Q}[a,b]/a^{2}$ . Returning to the homotopy fixed points spectral sequence, the above discussion implies that

$$ E_{2}^{\ast,\ast}\cong\mathbf{Q}[a,b][\![x_{1},\cdots,x_{4}]\!]/a^{2}. $$

There is a single differential

$$ d_{2}(a)=bx_{1}\overline{x_{1}}\cdots x_{4}\overline{x_{4}}, $$

and the spectral sequence is concentrated in even degrees after running this differential. It therefore collapses on the $E_{3}$ -page, and we find that there is an isomorphism

$$ \pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}[\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2}]^{hT^{4}}\cong\mathbf{Q}[b][\![x_{1},\cdots,x_{4}]\!]/bx_{1}\overline{x_{1}}\cdots x_{4}\overline{x_{4}}. $$

To calculate $\mathrm{H}^{T^{4}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})$ itself (and not just its completion $\pi_{\ast}\mathbf{Q}[\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2}]^{hT^{4}}$ ), the strategy of Theorem 4.2.13 reduces us to showing that the restriction $\mathrm{H}^{T^{4}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})|_{{\mathfrak{t}}^{\circ}}=\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{H}_{T^{4}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ . By Lemma 2.4.6, there is an isomorphism $\mathrm{H}^{T^{4}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})|_{{\mathfrak{t}}^{\circ}}\cong\mathrm{H}^{T^{4}}_{\ast}(\Omega(\mathbf{O}P^{2})^{T^{4}};\mathbf{Q})|_{{\mathfrak{t}}^{\circ}}$ . It therefore suffices to show that $\Omega(\mathbf{O}P^{2})^{T^{4}}$ is contractible, but this is a consequence of the simple observation that $(\mathbf{O}P^{2})^{T^{4}}\cong S^{0}$ . This discussion gives an isomorphism of graded $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{H}_{T^{4}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{T^{4}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathbf{Q}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{4},b]/bx_{1}\overline{x_{1}}\cdots x_{4}\overline{x_{4}}. $$

This isomorphism is $W$ -equivariant (where $W$ is the Weyl group of $\mathrm{Spin}_{9}$ ), so Proposition 2.3.15 implies that there is an isomorphism of graded $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Spin}_{9}}^{\ast}(\ast;\mathbf{Q})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{Spin}_{9}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{O}P^{2};\mathbf{Q})\cong\left(\mathbf{Q}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{4},b]/bx_{1}\overline{x}_{1}\cdots x_{4}\overline{x_{4}}\right)^{W}. $$

Noting that the action of $W$ leaves $b$ invariant, Lemma 4.6.4 computes the right-hand side; the resulting answer is precisely the right-hand side of the proposition. ∎

#### Lemma 4.9.2.

There is a homotopy equivalence $(\mathrm{Spin}_{7}/\mathrm{G}_{2})(\mathbf{C})\cong S^{7}$ , which implies that $(\mathrm{SO}_{7}/\mathrm{G}_{2})(\mathbf{C})\cong\mathbf{R}P^{7}$ . Moreover, if $B\subseteq G$ is the Borel subgroup of upper-triangular matrices, the Levi quotient $L(X)$ of the parabolic subgroup stabilizing the open $B$ -orbit in $\mathrm{SO}_{7}/\mathrm{G}_{2}$ is given by $\mathrm{GL}_{3}$ .

#### Lemma 4.9.3.

Let $W=\Sigma_{3}\times\mathbf{Z}/2$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ . Then there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{G}_{2}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[c_{2},c_{6}], $$

where the injective map $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{G}_{2}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\to\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{T^{2}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ sends

$$ \displaystyle c_{2} \displaystyle\mapsto x_{1}^{2}+x_{2}^{2}+x_{1}x_{2}, \displaystyle c_{6} \displaystyle\mapsto x_{1}^{2}x_{2}^{2}(x_{1}+x_{2})^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

The action of $\Sigma_{3}\subseteq W$ on $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{T^{2}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})=\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},x_{2}]$ is given by the reduced standard representation (i.e., $x_{1}$ , $x_{2}$ , and $-(x_{1}+x_{2})$ are permuted), and the action of $\mathbf{Z}/2\subseteq W$ is given by negating the $x_{i}$ simultaneously. It follows that

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{G}_{2}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})=\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{T^{2}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})^{W}\cong(\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},x_{2}]^{\Sigma_{3}})^{\mathbf{Z}/2}\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1}^{2}+x_{2}^{2}+x_{1}x_{2},x_{1}x_{2}(x_{1}+x_{2})]^{\mathbf{Z}/2}, $$

which is precisely $\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[c_{2},c_{6}]$ , as desired. ∎

#### Proposition 4.9.4.

There is an isomorphism of graded $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{\mathrm{G}_{2}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})$ -algebras

$$ \mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{G}_{2}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{R}P^{7};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},x_{2},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{x_{1}x_{2}x_{3}}]^{W}, $$

where $x_{3}=x_{1}+x_{2}$ is the sum of the two weights $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ . Here, the action of $\mathbf{Z}/2\subseteq W$ sends $x_{j}\mapsto-{x}_{j}$ and $a\mapsto a^{-1}$ , and the symmetric group acts by permuting the variables $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ (and leaves $a$ invariant).

#### Proof.

The restriction of the $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ -action on $(\mathrm{Spin}_{7}/\mathrm{G}_{2})(\mathbf{C})\simeq S^{7}$ exhibits it as the one-point compactification of $\mathrm{std}\oplus\mathbf{R}$ , where $\mathrm{std}$ is the standard $3$ -dimensional complex representation of $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ . In particular, the restriction of the $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ -action on $S^{7}$ to $T^{2}\subseteq\mathrm{G}_{2}$ exhibits it as the one-point compactification of the $3$ -dimensional representation of $T^{2}$ with weights $\lambda_{1}$ , $\lambda_{2}$ , and $\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2}$ . Given this observation, the isomorphism of the proposition is a consequence of Corollary 4.2.17 (just as with Proposition 4.6.5). ∎

#### Construction 4.9.5.

Let $W^{\prime}$ denote the Weyl group of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2}$ , so that $\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\cong\mathbf{A}^{1}(4)$ . Equip ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ with the grading by $-6\rho$ , and consider the ${\check{{G}}}_{X}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -scheme $\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ (where $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ acts only on the factor $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ by the adjoint action). Define

$$ {\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}=\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}}\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}). $$

Let $\kappa:\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W\to\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ denote the closed immersion sending

$$ (c_{2},c_{6})\mapsto c_{2},\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\
c_{6}&0\end{pmatrix}. $$

There is a closed immersion

$$ \displaystyle\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}) \displaystyle\cong\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}) \displaystyle\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathrm{Ind}_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}^{{\check{{G}}}}\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})\cong{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}, $$

and hence $\kappa$ defines a closed immersion

$$ \mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W\xrightarrow{{\kappa}}\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})\to{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}. $$

We will denote the above map by $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}}$ .

#### Proposition 4.9.6.

The ${\check{{G}}}$ -orbit of the image of $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}}$ has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ . Moreover, there is an isomorphism of graded group schemes over $\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W$ :

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{G}_{2}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{R}P^{7};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W. $$

In particular, the conditions of Theorem 3.6.4 hold for the spherical $\mathrm{SO}_{7}$ -variety $\mathrm{SO}_{7}/\mathrm{G}_{2}$ .

#### Proof.

Let us denote by $Y$ the $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -orbit of the image of $\kappa:\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W\to\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ . Then $Y\cong\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\mathrm{reg}}(6)$ , and it is well-known that the complement of $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\mathfrak{sl}_{2}$ has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ . Applying Lemma 4.3.10 to the $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -equivariant inclusion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})$ and the map $\mathrm{SL}_{2}\to{\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{Sp}_{6}$ , we conclude that the ${\check{{G}}}$ -orbit of the image of $\kappa_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}}$ has complement of codimension $\geq 2$ .

By Proposition 4.9.4, there is an isomorphism of graded schemes over $\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W$ :

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{G}_{2}}_{\ast}(\Omega\mathbf{R}P^{7};\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},x_{2},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{x_{1}x_{2}(x_{1}+x_{2})}]^{W}. $$

The action of $\Sigma_{3}\subseteq W$ on $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{T^{2}}(\ast;\mathbf{Z}^{\prime})=\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},x_{2}]$ is given by the reduced standard representation (i.e., $x_{1}$ , $x_{2}$ , and $-(x_{1}+x_{2})$ are permuted, and $a$ is fixed), and the action of $\mathbf{Z}/2\subseteq W$ is given by negating the $x_{i}$ simultaneously and sending $a\mapsto a^{-1}$ . It follows that

$$ \mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[x_{1},x_{2},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{x_{1}x_{2}(x_{1}+x_{2})}]^{W}\cong\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[c_{2},c_{6},a+a^{-1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{x_{1}x_{2}(x_{1}+x_{2})}]. $$

On the other hand, there is a graded isomorphism

$$ \displaystyle\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W \displaystyle\cong\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{(\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}}))/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-6\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W \displaystyle\cong\mathfrak{t}^{1}(2)/\!\!/W^{\prime}\times(\mathbf{A}^{1}(6)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)\times_{\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-6\rho)}\mathbf{A}^{1}(6)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)). $$

By construction, the map $\mathbf{A}^{1}(6)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)\cong\mathbf{A}^{1}(12)\to\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-6\rho)$ is precisely a shifted version of the Kostant slice, so the discussion in [Dev2, Remark B.4] implies that if we write $c_{6}$ to denote the coordinate on $\mathbf{A}^{1}(12)$ , there is an isomorphism

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{A}^{1}(6)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)\times_{\mathfrak{sl}_{2}(6-6\rho_{{\check{{G}}}_{X}})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-6\rho)}\mathbf{A}^{1}(6)/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2) \displaystyle\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[c_{3},a^{\pm 1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{x_{1}x_{2}(x_{1}+x_{2})}]^{\mathbf{Z}/2} \displaystyle\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[c_{6},a+a^{-1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{c_{3}}], $$

where $c_{3}^{2}=c_{6}$ . Therefore, there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W\times_{{\check{{M}}}^{\ddagger}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)}\mathfrak{t}^{2}(2)/\!\!/W\cong\spec\mathbf{Z}^{\prime}[c_{2},c_{6},a+a^{-1},\tfrac{a-a^{-1}}{x_{1}x_{2}(x_{1}+x_{2})}], $$

which gives the desired claim. ∎

#### Remark 4.9.7.

Using Proposition 4.9.4, one finds (by arguing as in Remark 4.6.8) that there is an isomorphism

$$ \spec\mathrm{H}^{\mathrm{SL}_{3}}_{\ast}(\Omega(\mathrm{SO}_{7}/\mathrm{G}_{2});\mathbf{Q})\cong\left(\mathbf{A}^{1}(6)\times_{\widetilde{\mathfrak{sl}_{2}}(6-6\rho)/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-6\rho)}\mathbf{A}^{1}(6)\right)\times\mathfrak{sp}_{2}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/\mathrm{Sp}_{2} $$

## 5. Structures on the spectral side

### 5.1. $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian spaces

Our goal in this section is to place the calculations of the preceding section into a broader context. The basic topic of study in this section is the $\beta$ -deformation of a group scheme introduced in Definition 3.7.3. We will soon focus on the graded quotient stack ${\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)_{\beta}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)$ appearing in Theorem 3.7.18.

#### Remark 5.1.1.

Since we will work in the setting of graded schemes, and both ${\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)_{\beta}$ and ${\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)$ are shifted by the same cocharacter of ${\check{{T}}}$ , we can (and will) simply ignore this cocharacter. In other words, we will focus only on the quotient stack ${\check{{G}}}_{\beta}/{\check{{G}}}$ , instead of ${\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)_{\beta}/{\check{{G}}}(-2\rho)$ .

We will begin with a brief review of the theory of shifted symplectic stacks; for optimal generality, we will work over a discrete commutative ring $R$ . Many of the results below were proved in [PTVV, Cal1, Saf1] under the assumption that $R$ is a $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebra, but this is often superfluous.

#### Recollection 5.1.2 ([PTVV, Cal1]).

Let $X$ be a derived $R$ -stack which admits a (co)tangent complex which is a perfect $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -module, and let $\mathrm{F}^{\star}_{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{dR}_{X/R}$ denote the Hodge-filtered de Rham complex of $X$ relative to $R$ , so that $\mathrm{gr}^{n}_{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{dR}_{X/R}=(\wedge^{n}L_{X/R})[-n]$ . A closed $j$ -form of degree $n$ on $X$ is a global section $\omega$ of $\mathrm{F}^{\geq j}_{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{dR}_{X/R}[n+j]$ ; let $\Omega^{j,\mathrm{cl}}_{BG/R,n}$ denote $\mathrm{H}^{0}(X;\mathrm{F}^{\geq j}_{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{dR}_{X/R}[n+j])$ . A closed $2$ -form $\omega$ of degree $n$ defines an $n$ -shifted symplectic structure on $X$ if the section of $(\wedge^{2}L_{X/R})[n]\simeq\Sym^{2}(L_{X/R}[1])[n-2]$ defined by the image of $\omega$ under the map

$$ \mathrm{F}^{\geq 2}_{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{dR}_{X/R}[n+2]\to\mathrm{gr}^{2}_{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{dR}_{X/R}[n+2]\cong(\wedge^{2}L_{X/R})[n] $$

defines an equivalence $T_{X/R}\xrightarrow{{\sim}}L_{X/R}[n]$ . If $X$ is an $n$ -shifted symplectic stack (the closed $2$ -form will be left implicit in the notation), let $\overline{X}$ denote $X$ equipped with the opposite symplectic structure.

Let $X$ be an $n$ -shifted symplectic stack, and let $f:L\to X$ be a morphism of derived $R$ -stacks, where $L$ and $f$ each admit perfect (co)tangent complexes. An isotropic structure on $f$ is a nullhomotopy of the composite

$$ T_{L}\to f^{\ast}T_{X}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\omega}}{{\simeq}}f^{\ast}L_{X}[n]\to L_{L}[n]. $$

An isotropic structure is called Lagrangian if the above composite is a cofiber sequence. If $X$ and $Y$ are $n$ -shifted symplectic stacks, a Lagrangian correspondence is a Lagrangian morphism $L\to X\times\overline{Y}$ . By [Saf1, Theorem 1.2], if $L_{1}\to X\times\overline{Y}$ and $L_{2}\to Y\times\overline{Z}$ are Lagrangian correspondences, the fiber product $L_{1}\times_{Y}L_{2}\to X\times\overline{Z}$ is also a Lagrangian correspondence. As a special case, if $L_{1},L_{2}\to X$ are Lagrangian morphisms to an $n$ -shifted symplectic stack, the fiber product $L_{1}\times_{X}L_{2}$ admits the structure of an $(n-1)$ -shifted symplectic stack.

#### Proposition 5.1.3.

Let $G$ be a split reductive group over $R$ , and assume that there is a nondegenerate $G$ -invariant quadratic form $q$ on $\mathfrak{g}$ . If its torsion primes are inverted in $R$ , any such $q$ on $\mathfrak{g}$ (more precisely, a choice of lift of $q$ along $\mathrm{H}^{4}_{\mathrm{dR}}(BG/R)\to\Sym^{2}(\mathfrak{g}^{\ast})^{G}$ , which does indeed exist) defines a $2$ -shifted symplectic structure on $BG$ .

#### Proof.

Any nondegenerate $G$ -invariant quadratic form $q$ on $\mathfrak{g}$ defines a section of $\mathrm{H}^{2}(BG;\wedge^{2}L_{BG/R})$ . The object $L_{BG/R}\in\mathrm{Perf}(BG)$ can be identified with the coadjoint representation $\mathfrak{g}^{\ast}[-1]$ . The underlying graded $R$ -algebra of the de Rham complex $\mathrm{dR}_{BG/R}$ can be identified with $\Gamma^{\ast}_{R}(L_{BG/R}[-1])\cong\Gamma^{\ast}_{R}(\mathfrak{g}^{\ast}[-2])$ . There is a décalage isomorphism $\Gamma^{n}_{R}(M[-2])\simeq\Sym^{n}_{R}(M)[-2n]$ for any bounded-below $R$ -module $M$ , and hence an isomorphism $\Gamma^{\ast}_{R}(\mathfrak{g}^{\ast}[-2])\cong\mathrm{sh}\Sym^{\ast}_{R}(\mathfrak{g}^{\ast}(-1))$ .

Now, the Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence runs

$$ E_{1}^{i,j}\cong\mathrm{H}^{j}(BG;\wedge^{i}L_{BG/R})\cong\mathrm{H}^{i-j}(G;\Sym^{i}(\mathfrak{g}^{\ast}))\Rightarrow\mathrm{H}^{i+j}_{\mathrm{dR}}(BG/R). $$

By [Tot, Theorem 10.2], the Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence for $BG$ degenerates at the $E_{1}$ -page since the torsion primes for $G$ are inverted in $R$ . Therefore, the map $\mathrm{H}^{4}(BG;\mathrm{F}^{\geq 2}_{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{dR}_{BG/R})\to\mathrm{H}^{2}(BG;\wedge^{2}L_{BG/R})$ is surjective, and any choice of a lift of $q$ along the map defines a closed $2$ -form of degree $2$ on $BG$ . It is easy to see that this closed $2$ -form defines a $2$ -shifted symplectic structure if and only if the associated $G$ -invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak{g}$ is nondegenerate. ∎

#### Remark 5.1.4.

Suppose $G$ is semisimple and simply-connected over $R=\mathbf{F}_{p}$ . Then $\mathfrak{g}$ admits a nondegenerate invariant quadratic form if and only if:

- • $p\nmid(n+1)$ if $G$ is of type $A_{n}$ (but $p$ can be arbitrary if $G=\mathrm{GL}_{n}$ );

- • $p\neq 2$ if $G$ is of type $B_{n}$ or $C_{n}$ with $n\geq 2$ , $D_{n}$ with $n\geq 4$ , $\mathrm{F}_{4}$ , or $\mathrm{E}_{7}$ ;

- • $p\neq 3$ if $G$ is of type $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ or $\mathrm{E}_{6}$ ;

- • $p$ arbitrary if $G$ is of type $\mathrm{E}_{8}$ .

Indeed, $p$ satisfies the above conditions if and only if $\mathfrak{g}$ admits a nondegenerate invariant symmetric bilinear form over $\mathbf{F}_{p}$ . See [Jan, Section 6.4(b)] and [GN2, Proposition 4] for a reference; in particular, the table following [GN2, Proposition 4] determines the order of the cokernel of the resulting map $\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbf{Z}}\to\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{\ast}$ . Since a quadratic form is nondegenerate when the same is true of its associated symmetric bilinear form (by definition), we only need to check that in each of these cases, the bilinear form admits a quadratic refinement. The relevant $G$ -invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak{g}$ is induced from the bilinear form $\langle{-,-}\rangle=\frac{1}{2h^{\vee}}\kappa(-,-)$ defined on $\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ , where $\kappa$ is the Killing form and $h^{\vee}$ is the dual Coxeter number. By [GN2, Proposition 4], the bilinear form $\langle{-,-}\rangle:\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbf{Z}}\times\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbf{Z}}\to\mathbf{Z}$ is even, and so it automatically admits a quadratic refinement as desired.

Looking at the torsion primes for $G$ , we see from Proposition 5.1.3 that $BG$ admits a $2$ -shifted symplectic structure over $\mathbf{F}_{p}$ if:

- • $2(n+1)\neq 0\pmod{p}$ if $G$ is of type $A_{n}$ (but $p$ can be arbitrary if $G=\mathrm{GL}_{n}$ );

- • $p\neq 2$ if $G$ is of type $B_{n}$ or $C_{n}$ with $n\geq 2$ , or $D_{n}$ with $n\geq 4$ ;

- • $p\neq 2,3$ if $G$ is of type $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ , $\mathrm{F}_{4}$ , $\mathrm{E}_{6}$ , or $\mathrm{E}_{7}$ ;

- • $p\neq 2,3,5$ if $G$ is of type $\mathrm{E}_{8}$ .

From now, all reductive groups $G$ over $R$ will be split, and we will assume that enough primes are inverted in $R$ so that the hypotheses of Proposition 5.1.3 are satisfied.

#### Proposition 5.1.5 ([PTVV, Theorem 2.5], [Saf1, Theorem 3.5]).

Let $X$ be an $d$ -oriented stack, i.e., a stack equipped with a map $\Gamma(X;\mathcal{O}_{X})\to R[-d]$ such that for any animated $R$ -algebra $A$ and any $\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Perf}(X\otimes_{R}A)$ , the induced map $\Gamma(X\otimes_{R}A;\mathcal{F})^{\vee}\to\Gamma(X\otimes_{R}A;\mathcal{F}[-d]^{\vee})$ is an isomorphism. The data of an $n$ -shifted symplectic structure on $Y$ equips the mapping stack $\mathrm{Map}(X,Y)$ with an $(n-d)$ -shifted symplectic structure. More generally, if $L\to Y$ is a Lagrangian morphism, the induced map $\mathrm{Map}(X,L)\to\mathrm{Map}(X,Y)$ acquires a natural Lagrangian structure.

#### Example 5.1.6.

Let $\mathbf{G}_{a}^{\sharp}(-2)$ denote the divided power hull of the origin in $\mathbf{G}_{a}$ equipped with a $\mathbf{G}_{m}$ -action placing its coordinate in weight $2$ , and let $\widehat{\mathbf{G}_{a}^{\sharp}(-2)}$ denote the completion of $\mathbf{G}_{a}^{\sharp}(-2)$ at the divided power filtration. Then $X=B\widehat{\mathbf{G}_{a}^{\sharp}(-2)}$ is a $1$ -oriented stack: the cohomology of its structure sheaf is isomorphic to $R[\epsilon]/\epsilon^{2}$ with $\epsilon$ in homological degree $-1$ (and weight $-2$ ). Moreover, if $Y$ is any derived $R$ -stack which admits a cotangent complex, and ${T_{Y}^{\sharp}(2)}$ denotes the PD-hull of the zero section of the tangent bundle of $Y$ , the mapping stack $\mathrm{Map}(B\widehat{\mathbf{G}_{a}^{\sharp}(-2)},Y)$ can be identified with the stack ${BT_{Y}^{\sharp}(2)}$ . It follows from Proposition 5.1.5 that the data of an $n$ -shifted symplectic structure on $Y$ equips ${BT_{Y}^{\sharp}(2)}$ with an $(n-1)$ -shifted symplectic structure.

Let $G$ be a reductive group over $R$ equipped with a nondegenerate $G$ -invariant quadratic form on $\mathfrak{g}$ . When $Y=BG$ , we may identify $T_{BG}\cong\mathfrak{g}[1]\in\mathrm{Perf}(BG)$ , which implies that ${BT_{BG}^{\sharp}(2)}\cong\mathfrak{g}(2)/G$ . It follows from Proposition 5.1.3 that $\mathfrak{g}(2)/G$ admits a $1$ -shifted symplectic structure of weight $2$ ; forgetting the grading, we see that $\mathfrak{g}/G$ admits a $1$ -shifted symplectic structure.

#### Example 5.1.7.

Let $S^{1}$ denote the constant stack $B\mathbf{Z}$ . Then $S^{1}$ is a $1$ -oriented stack, since $\Gamma(S^{1};\mathcal{O})\cong C^{\ast}(S^{1};R)$ , and the circle admits a canonical orientation. It follows from Proposition 5.1.5 that the data of an $n$ -shifted symplectic structure on $Y$ equips $\mathrm{Map}(S^{1},Y)$ with an $(n-1)$ -shifted symplectic structure. In particular, if $G$ is a reductive group over $R$ , then applying Proposition 5.1.3 implies that $\mathrm{Map}(S^{1},BG)\cong G/G$ admits a $1$ -shifted symplectic structure.

#### Proposition 5.1.8 ([Saf1]).

Let $R=\mathbf{C}$ , and let $G$ be a complex reductive group. A Lagrangian morphism $L\to\mathfrak{g}/G$ is equivalent to the data of a Hamiltonian $G$ -space. Similarly, a Lagrangian morphism $L\to G/G$ is equivalent to the data of a quasi-Hamiltonian $G$ -space in the sense of [AMM].

The reader not familiar with the definition of a quasi-Hamiltonian $G$ -space can take the second part of Proposition 5.1.8 to be a definition. Motivated by Lemma 3.7.4, we make the following observation.

#### Lemma 5.1.9.

The stack $B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ admits a canonical $1$ -orientation of weight $2$ .

#### Proof.

We will just construct the orientation on $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ , and leave verifying the properties of Proposition 5.1.5 to the reader. To compute the cohomology $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})$ , let us first compute $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ . As shown in [Dev3, Proposition C.6], the Cartier dual $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ is isomorphic to $\spf\mathbf{Z}[\beta,\frac{1}{n!}\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(y-j\beta)]^{\wedge}$ where the element $y$ is primitive (i.e., the coproduct sends $y\mapsto y\otimes 1+1\otimes y$ ) and lives in weight $2$ . Here, the completion is taken with respect to the $\beta$ -deformed divided power filtration (i.e., with respect to $\frac{1}{n!}\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(y-j\beta)$ for $n\geq 1$ ). Computing the cohomology of the trivial $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ -representation in the standard manner shows that $\mathrm{H}^{0}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})\cong R$ , $\mathrm{H}^{1}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})$ is isomorphic to the submodule of primitive elements in $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}}$ , and $\mathrm{H}^{j}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})$ is zero for $j>1$ . It is not difficult to see that the only primitive elements in $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}}$ are scalar multiples of $y$ , and so the cohomology ring $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})$ is exterior on a single class in cohomological degree $1$ and weight $2$ . This generator of $\mathrm{H}^{1}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})$ gives the desired $1$ -orientation of $B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ . ∎

#### Remark 5.1.10.

The $1$ -orientation on $B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ is closely connected to the preorientation on $\mathbf{G}_{\beta,\mathrm{ku}}$ from Proposition 2.3.11. Indeed, the $1$ -orientation on $B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ can be viewed as a map $B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}\to B\mathbf{G}_{a}$ . Since there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{Map}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},B\mathbf{G}_{a})\cong\Hom(\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},\mathbf{G}_{a})/\mathbf{G}_{a}\cong\Hom(\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},\mathbf{G}_{a})\times B\mathbf{G}_{a}, $$

we can identify

$$ \mathrm{H}^{1}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})\cong\pi_{0}\mathrm{Map}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},B\mathbf{G}_{a})\cong\pi_{0}\Hom(\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},\mathbf{G}_{a}), $$

and the $1$ -orientation on $B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}$ can be viewed as a homomorphism $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee}\to\mathbf{G}_{a}$ . However, $\Hom(\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},\mathbf{G}_{a})$ is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ , and a section of this Lie algebra is precisely the datum of a preorientation on $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ .

#### Proposition 5.1.11.

Let $G$ be a reductive group over $R$ . The choice of a nondegenerate $G$ -invariant quadratic form on $\mathfrak{g}$ equips $\mathrm{Map}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},BG)\cong G_{\beta}/G$ with a $1$ -shifted symplectic structure of weight $2$ . If $G$ is semisimple and $G^{\prime}$ is centrally isogenous of $G$ 2727 27 For instance, $G$ is simply-connected and $G^{\prime}=G/Z(G)$ ; or $G$ is adjoint and $G^{\prime}$ is the natural $\pi_{1}(G)_{\mathrm{tors}}$ -cover., the quotient stack $G^{\prime}_{\beta}/G$ admits a $1$ -shifted symplectic structure of weight $2$ .

#### Proof.

This is a consequence of Proposition 5.1.3, Proposition 5.1.5, and Lemma 5.1.9. ∎

#### Definition 5.1.12.

Let $G$ be a reductive group over $R$ . Let $M$ be a graded $R[\beta]$ -stack which admits a cotangent complex, and suppose $M$ is equipped with a $G$ -action. A $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian structure on $M$ is a Lagrangian morphism $M/G\to G_{\beta}/G$ . The resulting $G$ -equivariant map $M\to G_{\beta}$ will be called the $\mathrm{ku}$ -moment map. If $G$ is semisimple, a slight variant of this definition would be to ask for a Lagrangian morphism $M/G\to G_{\beta}/G$ ; we will sometimes refer to such data also as a $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian structure on $M$ .

#### Remark 5.1.13.

Motivated by Lemma 3.7.2, one alternative name for $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian structures might be “HKR-filtered quasi-Hamiltonian structures” (where HKR stands for Hochschild-Kostant-Rosenberg).

#### Remark 5.1.14.

As in Remark 3.7.5, it is not really crucial to treat $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ as the fundamental object here: we could have considered any $1$ -dimensional group scheme over $\mathbf{Z}[\beta]$ in place of $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ . Suppose we permit $1$ -dimensional formal group schemes. Fix a prime $p$ , let $\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{k_{\mathbf{Z}}(n)}$ be the $1$ -dimensional formal group over $\mathbf{Z}_{(p)}[\beta]$ from Remark 3.7.5, and let $G$ be a reductive group over $\mathbf{Z}_{(p)}[\beta]$ . One can then prove that $\mathrm{Map}(B\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{k_{\mathbf{Z}}(n)}^{\vee},BG)$ admits a $1$ -shifted symplectic structure over $\mathbf{Z}_{(p)}[\beta]$ ; Lagrangian morphisms to this stack provide a(n integral) Morava K-theoretic analogue of $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian spaces. Again, we will not study these objects further in the present article, but we hope to in [Dev5].

#### Remark 5.1.15.

In the setting of differential geometry (as studied in [AMM]), where $G$ is replaced by a compact Lie group, [AMM, Theorem 8.3] proves that there is an equivalence between quasi-Hamiltonian $G$ -spaces and Hamiltonian $LG$ -spaces (the latter needing some care to define because of infinite-dimensional analytic issues). It seems likely that the notion of a $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian structure in the setting of differential geometry might be equivalent to the theory of Hamiltonian spaces for $\mathrm{Map}(S^{1}_{\beta},G)$ , with $S^{1}_{\beta}$ being defined as

$$ S^{1}_{\beta}=\{(\beta,z)|\|z\|=\beta\}\subseteq\mathbf{R}\times\mathbf{C}, $$

and the $\mathrm{Map}(S^{1}_{\beta},G)$ -Hamiltonian space is equipped with a compatible fibration to $\mathbf{R}$ . In other words, the radii of the fibers of $S^{1}_{\beta}\to\mathbf{R}$ should be related to the parameter $\beta$ .

#### Proposition 5.1.16.

Let $P\subseteq G$ be a parabolic subgroup, let $U_{P}\subseteq P$ denote its unipotent radical, and let $L=P/U_{P}$ denote the Levi quotient. Then $\mathrm{Ind}_{U_{P}}^{G}P_{\beta}$ admits the structure of a $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian $G\times L$ -space where the $\mathrm{ku}$ -moment map $\mathrm{Ind}_{U_{P}}^{G}P_{\beta}\to G_{\beta}$ is given by conjugation.

#### Proof.

As shown in [Saf1, Lemma 3.4], the maps $BP\to BG$ and $BP\to BL$ define a Lagrangian correspondence $BP\to BG\times BL$ , essentially because there is an exact sequence

$$ 0\to\mathfrak{p}\to\mathfrak{g}\oplus\mathfrak{l}\to\mathfrak{p}^{\ast}\to 0. $$

It follows from Proposition 5.1.5 and Lemma 5.1.9 that there is a Lagrangian correspondence

$$ P_{\beta}/P\cong\mathrm{Map}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},BP)\to\mathrm{Map}(B\mathbf{G}_{\beta}^{\vee},BG\times BL)\cong G_{\beta}/G\times L_{\beta}/L. $$

Since $P_{\beta}/P\times_{BG\times BL}\spec\mathbf{Z}[\beta]\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{U_{P}}^{G}P_{\beta}$ , this produces the desired $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian $G\times L$ -structure on $\mathrm{Ind}_{U_{P}}^{G}P_{\beta}$ . ∎

#### Remark 5.1.17.

Upon inverting $\beta$ and quotienting by $\mathbf{G}_{m}$ , Proposition 5.1.16 reduces to [Boa, Theorem 9].

#### Proposition 5.1.18.

Let $B\subseteq G$ be a Borel subgroup with unipotent radical $N$ . Then $\mathrm{Ind}_{N}^{G}B_{\beta}$ admits the structure of a $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian $G$ -space, where the $\mathrm{ku}$ -moment map $\mathrm{Ind}_{N}^{G}B_{\beta}\to G_{\beta}$ is given by conjugation.

#### Proof.

Let us first show show that the map $(\mathrm{Ind}_{N}^{G}B_{\beta})/G\cong B_{\beta}/N\to G_{\beta}/G$ admits a Lagrangian structure. Using Proposition 5.1.16, Recollection 5.1.2, and the isomorphism $B_{\beta}/B\times_{G_{\beta}/G\times T_{\beta}/T}(G_{\beta}/G\times T_{\beta})\cong B_{\beta}/N$ , it suffices to show that the map $T_{\beta}\to T_{\beta}/T$ is a Lagrangian morphism. For this, note that the tangent complex to $H_{\beta}/H$ is given by the complex $\underline{\mathfrak{h}}\to T_{H_{\beta}}$ , where $\underline{\mathfrak{h}}$ denotes $\mathfrak{h}\otimes\mathcal{O}_{H_{\beta}}$ , and the differential $\mathfrak{h}\to\Gamma(H_{\beta};\mathcal{O})$ is given by the adjoint action $\xi\mapsto\xi^{R}-\xi^{L}$ . Here, $\xi^{L}$ and $\xi^{R}$ denote the vector fields generating the left and right actions of $H$ on $H_{\beta}$ . (Note that there is an isomorphism $T_{H_{\beta}}\cong\underline{\mathfrak{h}}$ .) When $H$ is commutative (such as $H=T$ ), $\xi^{R}=\xi^{L}$ , and so the tangent complex is split. There is an obvious cofiber sequence

$$ \underline{\mathfrak{t}}\to\underline{\mathfrak{t}}\oplus\underline{\mathfrak{t}}[1]\to\underline{\mathfrak{t}}[1], $$

which identifies with the cofiber sequence

$$ T_{T_{\beta}}\to T_{T_{\beta}/T}\cong L_{T_{\beta}/T}\to L_{T_{\beta}}[1]. $$

This gives the desired Lagrangian structure. ∎

#### Remark 5.1.19.

Suppose $G=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ , so that the affine closure of $G/N\cong\mathrm{SL}_{2}/\mathbf{G}_{a}\cong\mathbf{A}^{2}-\{0\}$ is smooth. Using the algebraic Hartogs lemma, one can show that the $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian structure on the $G$ -space $\mathrm{Ind}_{N}^{G}B_{\beta}\cong\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times^{\mathbf{G}_{a}}B_{\beta}$ from Proposition 5.1.18 extends to a $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian structure on its affine closure $\overline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times^{\mathbf{G}_{a}}B_{\beta}}$ . It seems reasonable to expect that this is true in general, i.e., that the $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian structure on the $G$ -space $\mathrm{Ind}_{N}^{G}B_{\beta}$ from Proposition 5.1.18 extends to $\overline{\mathrm{Ind}_{N}^{G}B_{\beta}}$ . This is not immediately clear from the perspective of derived algebraic geometry, since neither of the affine closures $\overline{G/N}$ or $\overline{\mathrm{Ind}_{N}^{G}B_{\beta}}$ are smooth outside of the rank one case.

For the sake of concreteness, let us describe the affine closure $\overline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times^{\mathbf{G}_{a}}B_{\beta}}$ explicitly. Fix $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ and $(x,y)\in B_{\beta}$ with $a$ , $d$ , and $y$ in weight $0$ , $c$ and $x$ in weight $-2$ , and $b$ in weight $2$ . Then the action of $\begin{pmatrix}1&z\\ 0&1\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbf{G}_{a}$ (with $z$ in weight $2$ ) sends

$$ \begin{pmatrix}a&b\\
c&d\end{pmatrix}\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}a&az+b\\
c&cz+d\end{pmatrix},\ (x,y)\mapsto(x,y+z[-2](x)), $$

where $[-2](x)=-\frac{\beta x^{2}+2x}{1+\beta x}$ is the $(-2)$ -series of $x$ in the group law on $\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ . In particular, the $\mathbf{G}_{a}$ -action fixes $a$ , $c$ , and $x$ , as well as $ay-[-2](x)b$ and $cy-[-2](x)d$ . If we write $B=ay-[-2](x)b$ (in weight $0$ ) and $D=cy-[-2](x)d$ (in weight $-2$ ), the only relation is

$$ cB-aD=[-2](x). $$

In other words, $\overline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times^{\mathbf{G}_{a}}B_{\beta}}$ is cut out inside $\mathbf{A}^{4}_{\mathbf{Z}[\beta]}\times_{\spec\mathbf{Z}[\beta]}\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ by the above equation, where the affine space has coordinates $a,c,B,D$ .

If we had instead replaced the $\mathbf{G}_{a}$ -action on $B_{\beta}$ by conjugation with the $\mathbf{G}_{a}$ -action on ${\check{{V}}}_{\beta}=\mathbf{A}^{1}\times\mathbf{G}_{\beta}$ (following the notation of Construction 4.3.11 with $n=1$ ), the above equations would continue to hold if $[-2](x)$ was replaced by $\overline{x}$ . The analogue of the equation 5.1 implies that $\overline{x}=cB-aD$ , so $\overline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times^{\mathbf{G}_{a}}V_{\beta}}$ is the open subscheme of $\mathbf{A}^{4}_{\mathbf{Z}[\beta]}$ given by the complement of the hypersurface

$$ 1+\beta(cB-aD)=0. $$

Note that when $\beta=0$ , this is the entirety of $\mathbf{A}^{4}$ . Just as with $\overline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times^{\mathbf{G}_{a}}B_{\beta}}$ , the scheme $\overline{\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times^{\mathbf{G}_{a}}V_{\beta}}$ also admits a $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian structure for its natural $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -action, and perhaps deserves to be called $T^{\ast}_{\beta}\mathbf{A}^{2}$ .

#### Remark 5.1.20.

If $H\subseteq G$ is a closed subgroup, it is natural to ask whether there is a “ $\mathrm{ku}$ -theoretic” cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}_{\beta}(G/H)$ whose fiber at $\beta=0$ is $T^{\ast}(G/H)$ , and which admits the structure of a $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian $G$ -space? It seems rather difficult to define such an object for arbitrary subgroups $H$ . However, in the case that the annhilator of ${\mathfrak{h}}\subseteq\mathfrak{g}$ (under an invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak{g}$ ) is itself a Lie subalgebra, we expect this to be possible, but we will not study this topic here. (For instance, Proposition 5.1.18 fits into this general class of examples.) Upon inverting $\beta$ , i.e., working with quasi-Hamiltonian $G$ -spaces, this was shown in [BM].
